title: feat(ui): edit a tool in the tool library window
body:
Stacked on #3900 (U1). The base is `main`, because #3900 is a fork branch. The diff of U2 alone: https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/be7168455...issue/3893-tool-library-editor

## What changed

U2 of #3663: you edit a tool in the tool library window.

- A tool opens in the window's editor. The list folds into a rail on the left ("All tools" and one row for each tool).
- The editor has two tabs:
  - **Tool**: the type, the geometry and the kind rows. The tab calls `tool_settings_grid::geometry` (with `kind_rows`). It does not copy them.
  - **Details**: the material group, the catalog facts of #898 and the tool number. The tab calls `tool_settings_grid::catalog` (with `tool_catalog_rows::catalog_rows`).
- **Apply** queues the same commands as the Apply of Properties: `State::apply_tool_numbers` (`ChangeTool`, or `ReshapeTool` when a drawn cutter rides the change) and `push_number_if_changed` (`SetToolNumber`, only when the number changed). A geometry and catalog edit is one undo step.
- **Edit tool shape** opens the existing shape window. That window edits through the draft of Properties. Thus, when Properties shows a different tool, Properties first moves to the tool of the window.
- The window keeps its **own draft** (`ToolLibraryView::editor`). Properties keeps `State::tool_ui`. `State::with_library_draft` swaps the draft of the window (and its sync key) into `tool_ui` only while the window draws and applies. Each draft has its own `(name, doc_version)` key, so typing in one draft never resets the other.
- The "Edit" button of the Document list opens the tool in the window. A new window opens on the tool that Properties shows. A pick in the window does not change the selection or the subject of Properties.
- If the open tool goes out of the document, the editor closes and the full list shows again.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3893-tool-library-editor.md`.

No new command. No MCP tool is owed. Properties keeps all its groups. The holder, the cutting data and the drawing come to the window in U3 to U5.

## Readings

- `crates/ui` lib: 1,595 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored. The `#[test]` count goes up by 4. No test was removed or ignored.
- No snapshot PNG changed. No `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` changed. Each new file has fewer than 170 lines.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::tool_library_editor::apply_is_one_change_tool_and_undo_restores`
- `egui_app::tests::tool_library_editor::the_dialog_draft_and_the_properties_draft_do_not_mix`
- `egui_app::tests::tool_library_editor::details_tab_shows_the_catalog_facts`
- `egui_app::tests::page_layout_tool_library::layout_window_tool_editor`

## Gate (Windows, winbuild, trial merge of head bae9b7b5a with origin/main 1e182f2cf)

- Targeted: the four pinning tests and `layout_window_tool_library`: pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 18 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall time 5.2 min. The steps were the ui build, `ui suites: lib` and 16 ui suites (boundary, boundary_picks, catalog_render, contour_dxf_sketch, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_example, theme_files, waterjet_tool).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass.
- No post, toolpath or geometry changed. Thus no `example_catalog*` suite is necessary, and the light lane reaches no step.
- An earlier gate run on head 5c7c79cd0 failed on a wrong import path in the new test file (`egui_kittest::Node`). The fix is commit 407680617.

## Not exercised

- A real typing session in the running app. The tests set the drafts directly and click Apply, Details and the rail through AccessKit.
- The shape window opened from the editor, while Properties shows a different tool. The code path is short, but no test pins it.
- macOS and Linux builds.

## Screenshots

Rendered without a window with egui_kittest, from a scratch test that is not committed.

| | Before (U1 head be7168455) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Window open | ![before list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3893/before-1-list.png) | ![after list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3893/after-1-list.png) |
| "Edit" on a tool | ![before edit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3893/before-2-edit.png) | ![after edit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3893/after-2-edit.png) |
| Details tab | - | ![after details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3893/after-3-details.png) |

Changelog: Edit a tool's geometry and catalog facts in the tool library window. Apply is one undo step.

title: feat(ui): the Tools ribbon cell opens a tool library window
body:
U1 of #3663: the tool library leaves the dock and opens in its own window.

## What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library_dialog/mod.rs`: `tool_library_window(ctx, state)`. It is a non-modal in-app `egui::Window` with the id `tool-library` and the title "Tool library". It follows the pattern of the tool shape window. It opens left of the Properties pane, so the user can use the two at the same time.
- New `tool_library_dialog/list.rs`: the tools list. The body of `egui_app/tool_library.rs` moved here, and that file is deleted. The labels "Tool type", "Name filter", "New tool…", "Export library…", "Import library…", "Import tool holders" and "Catalog" do not change.
  - Two sources: "Document" and "Catalog". A new window opens on Document when the document has tools, else on Catalog.
  - The Document list shows the columns of #3663: T, Tool, Kind, Ø, Flute length, Flutes, Holder, Recipes. "Edit" shows the tool in Properties.
  - The Catalog rows keep their label form and their "Add" button.
  - The Tool type and Name filters apply to the two sources.
- New `crates/ui/src/state_tool_library_dialog.rs`: `ToolLibraryView { source }` and `ToolSource`. `state.rs` gets one field (`tool_library`), the `mod` line and its `pub use`.
- `actions::target` with the empty tool name opens the window and keeps `ui_target`. The four doors use it: the ribbon Tools cell, the View menu "Tool library…", and the gate route for "no tool" and for "no fitting tool".
- `LayoutRequest::ToolLibrary` is removed. `shell.rs` draws the window after the tool shape window. `Tab::Tools` draws nothing.
- The `Tab::Tools` variant stays, because a saved panel setup can name it. `layout::setups::decode` removes the tab on load. It also removes a float that held only that tab.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3892-tool-library-shell.md`.

Commands: none new. "Add" uses `AddTool`. Import uses `ImportTools`. Opening and closing the window is view state, as for the tool shape window. No MCP tool is owed.

## Readings

- The window opens at 20 % of the screen width and 15 % of its height, at 620 × (70 % of the screen height). At 1280 × 720 it does not touch the Properties leaf (pinned).
- `#[test]` count of `crates/ui`: 1768 on `origin/main`, 1770 on this head. One test moved (`layout_page_tool_library` is now `layout_window_tool_library`). Two tests are new.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::page_layout_tool_library::layout_window_tool_library` (new file; `page_layout.rs` is full): the window is open after a click on Tools, its anchors stack top to bottom, and it does not cover Properties.
- `egui_app::tests::page_layout_tool_library::the_tool_library_window_closes_and_opens_again`.
- `egui_app::tests::panel_setups::a_saved_setup_with_the_old_tool_library_tab_still_loads`.
- I ran the first and the third test red on the test-only commit `0604ed8f8` before the change (2 failed: the window was not open; the old tab stayed in the dock).

Tests updated, none deleted:
- `tool_properties::tools_ribbon_opens_the_tool_library_window_without_retargeting_properties` (was `..._opens_a_docked_catalog_...`).
- `tool_properties::browser_library_door_opens_the_window_and_tool_selection_focuses_properties` (was `..._focus_their_own_dock_tabs`). The window now stays open when a tool is selected.
- `tool_icon_wiring::every_catalog_row_paints_its_kind_glyph`: it selects the Catalog source first.
- `gate_route_tests::no_tool_routes_to_the_tool_library`, the drill gate test in `tests.rs`, `panel_setups::arrange` (the float holds Debug info now), the header of `page_layout.rs`, and the Gate maps of `catalog_filters.rs` and `edm_tool_visibility.rs`.

## Gate (Windows, host winbuild, head `be7168455`)

The Mac build lane belongs to a different agent. All builds and tests ran on the Windows machine winbuild, with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1` and `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 18 steps, 18 ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 5.2 min. Steps: ui build, ui lib (115 s), and the ui suites boundary, boundary_picks, catalog_render, contour_dxf_sketch, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_example, theme_files, waterjet_tool. The plan is larger than 10 steps because `state.rs` and `actions.rs` reach more ui suites. The issue expected 10 to about 20.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.

## What was not exercised

- The light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): not run. Its dry run lists only `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-app` twins, and this diff touches `crates/ui` only.
- No heavy lane (not a `P1`).
- The example catalog suites: not run. No post or toolpath changed.
- No snapshot PNG changed. The release-lane pixel snapshots of the shell do not open the tool library, so I expect no change there. They run at the cut.
- I did not test the window by hand in the native app. The screenshots below come from the egui_kittest harness.

title: fix(motion): warn on start-side stand-in entries and a Plunge into stock
body:
## What changed

A plain 2D Pocket with "Pass starts at: Outside" and no stock known has no air room (#3746). Before this change, two entries were notes only:

- With Arc, a later pass start in material took a ramp along the pass (`descent_dive::entry_restart`).
- With Plunge, the pass link plunged into uncut stock with no note.

`entry_status_lines` dropped the notes, and no warning was posted.

Now, on a start-side ladder (`Motion::cleared_links`, the #3316 link law):

- Each named stand-in entry (a ramp, a helix, an axial dive or a plunge) writes the marker `ENTRY_STAND_IN_NOTE`. The op posts one advisory `Warning::EntryStandIn { at, entries }` that counts the stand-ins.
- A pass link that plunges into a pass start in material writes `PLUNGE_INTO_STOCK_NOTE`. The op posts one advisory `Warning::PlungeIntoStock`. If the op already posts `EntryNotRecommended` for the selected Plunge, it does not post this second warning. Thus the plunge is named once.
- `entry_status_lines` shows each stand-in note as a `warning: Entry: ... - fix: ...` line. The two marker notes add no line, because the op warning is already in the status area.
- MCP names the new kinds `entry_stand_in` and `plunge_into_stock`.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3884-start-side-entry-warnings.md`. Arc with no air room keeps a safe, named stand-in with a Warning. It does not refuse, because a refusal would refuse every plain Outside pocket that uses the default Arc and has no stock.

The new code is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/entry_warn.rs`. The changes to `generate.rs` and `types.rs` add only a few lines each. Both files were already over 400 lines.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_engagement::outside_pocket_arc_ramp_is_a_warning` (pin 1): the band pocket with no stock and Arc has named stand-ins, and has exactly one `EntryStandIn` warning that counts them.
- `pass_start_engagement::outside_pocket_plunge_into_stock_is_one_warning` (pin 2): the same pocket with Plunge has more than one plunge, and has exactly one warning that names the plunge.
- `camcraft-ui` lib `approach_page::top_stock_tests::each_stand_in_entry_is_a_warning_line` (pin 3): the four stand-in note forms from the review are warning lines.

Red first: the pins use the new API (`entry_warnings`, `entry_stand_ins`, the marker notes), so they do not compile on `main`. Without the API, main has no warning and no status line for these notes. The review of #3872 proved this with a probe.

## Gates

- Targeted pins: green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 324 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (76.7 min); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Heavy steps (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: offset_pass_start"` ok (1146 s); `--only "app heavy: pocket_pass_start"` ok (10 s).

## Not exercised

- No app-level test that reads the op warnings for this pocket. The op adds the result of `entry_warnings` with one line in `generate.rs`.
- The stand-ins of Auto ladders show as warning lines on the op page, but they post no op warning (out of scope; see the decision).

Changelog: A 2D Pocket with "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside now posts a warning for each entry that is not the selected one, and for a selected Plunge that plunges into uncut stock. Before, these were notes only.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #3884

title: fix(motion): refuse a Ramp or Helix entry under control or wear compensation
body:
## What changed

- `contour_comp::door` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_comp.rs`) refuses a 2D Contour under control or wear compensation when the entry or the level transition is Ramp or Helix. The refusal names the mode and the arm, for example: "control compensation does not ride a Ramp entry - its descent runs on the lead-in and the ring before G41/G42 engages, so the register does not apply to it; pick the Plunge or Arc entry, or Computer compensation".
- The rule applies to the wall side and to the bore side. It is checked from the parameters, before any geometry.
- Computer compensation is unchanged.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3888-ramp-comp-refusal.md`. The refusal was chosen over a ramp inside the G41/G42 span (a new span shape and proof) and over a ramp on the lead-in only (its last leg still touches the wall under G40).

## Why

G41/G42 engages on the lead-in move that lands on the ring. The wall-side zig-zag (PR #3833) and the bore side's zig-zag, orbit and dive links run before that move, under G40, at the nominal centre. A register larger than the nominal radius, or a positive wear value, cut the finished wall there, and the verifier did not see it.

## Pinning tests (red on main, green here)

- `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs` `a_ramp_or_helix_under_control_or_wear_is_refused_by_name_on_both_sides`: Control and Wear; Side::Outside and Side::Inside (bore); Ramp and Helix entry; Ramp transition. Each is refused by name. Plunge still generates its spans. Red on main: the generation succeeded.
- `crates/app/tests/control_comp.rs` `a_ramp_or_helix_before_g41_under_control_or_wear_is_refused_and_posts_nothing`: through `GenerateOperation`, Control and Wear, Outside and Auto, Ramp and Helix. Each is refused by name, no toolpath is stored, and the post gate writes no G41/G42 program. Red on main: the generation succeeded.
- Computer compensation is unchanged: `a_wall_side_ramp_in_computer_compensation_is_unchanged` (motion: the same moves as the default ramp, no span) and `a_wall_side_ramp_in_computer_posts_its_ramp_without_comp_words` (app: the zig-zag stands, and the Fanuc post writes no G41/G42).

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6): 18 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes the motion suites `lib`, `climb_direction`, `contour_start_comp`, `control_comp`, `machining2d`, `wear_comp`, and the app suites `control_comp` and `example_catalog*`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy: the touched test binaries have no `#[ignore]` heavy tests, so no targeted heavy step applies. The full heavy lanes were not run.

## Not exercised

- The app pin does not cover Side::Inside: a whole-model source refuses Side::Inside before generation. The door reads only the parameters, so the motion pin holds the bore side.
- The bore side's Plunge and Arc entries, and the wall side's Arc entry, still run before G41/G42 at the nominal radius. Their dive at the lead-in start or their arc in the air was not changed and was not measured against a register over the nominal radius.

Changelog: A 2D Contour under control or wear compensation now refuses a Ramp or Helix entry (or level transition) by name; the ramp ran on the ring before G41/G42 engaged and could cut the wall.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #3888

title: fix(post): refuse waterjet posting until the jet records exist
body:
## What changed

This PR takes option 1 of the issue. It refuses waterjet posting by name until the jet records (#1882) and the waterjet laws (#1885) exist.

- The post gate (`verification_report_by`) refuses each unsuppressed waterjet operation. The new clause is in `crates/app/src/posting_waterjet.rs`. The refusal names the missing items: the standoff height, the jet on/off records, the pierce dwell records and the waterjet laws.
- A user post that declares `serves = ["waterjet"]` goes through the same gate. It writes no NC file.
- The stock simulation skips waterjet operations, as it skips wire cuts (`crates/app/src/stock_sim_waterjet.rs`). The nozzle does not go into the dexel model or the stock playback.
- The program sim refuses its verdict by name: "waterjet stock removal is not judged". The post gate shows this on its visible not-judged line.
- The path notes say that the jet and dwell records are not implemented. They also give a note for a pierce on the kerf ring when the lead-in is zero.
- The waterjet page:
  - shows the zero lead-in consequence;
  - shows the compensation choice as "In control" (no G-code words);
  - gives each tab row its own name ("Tab 1 position").
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/3637-waterjet-safety.md`. It also records that the operation does not model corner slow-down, taper or kerf lag.

## Cause

The waterjet operation has no standoff height. Its CL has no jet on/off record and no dwell record. No law refused it. A user post that served waterjet got a path with the nozzle tip at the sheet top. The stock sim used the nozzle as a milling cutter, and no note said that it does not judge waterjet.

## Note on the first attempt

The first attempt failed `post_not_judged::not_judged_with_no_generator_verdict_blocks` two times. Its waterjet clause sent back the generic `program_ops` error. The sim clause already reports that error, so the gate named one fault two times. Now the waterjet clause adds nothing when the program list cannot be read.

## Tests

Pins (`crates/app/tests/waterjet_profile.rs`):
- `waterjet_post_gate_names_the_missing_safety_records`
- `waterjet_user_post_cannot_bypass_the_safety_refusal`
- `waterjet_stock_verdict_is_refused_by_name`
- `waterjet_nozzle_is_absent_from_stock_playback`
- `waterjet_verification_reports_the_unjudged_operation`
- `waterjet_zero_lead_in_reports_the_pierce_on_the_kerf_ring`
- `waterjet_safety_refusal_omits_suppressed_operations_and_empty_documents` (control: green before and after)

Pins (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/waterjet_ribbon_tests.rs`):
- `waterjet_compensation_uses_a_plain_control_label`
- `waterjet_tab_position_rows_have_unique_names`
- `waterjet_zero_lead_in_names_the_part_edge_pierce`

Existing pin for the duplicate error: `post_not_judged::not_judged_with_no_generator_verdict_blocks`.

Mutation checks:
1. I put back the old `posting.rs`, `stock_sim.rs` and `waterjet/emit.rs`. Six app pins failed. The control passed. I restored the files. All 13 tests passed.
2. I put back the old `Err(why) => return vec![why]` arm. `not_judged_with_no_generator_verdict_blocks` failed with `left: 2, right: 1`. I restored the arm. The test passed.
3. I put back the old `waterjet_page.rs`. The three UI pins failed. I restored the file. The pins passed.

Original author gate runs (base `f2aa981b5`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 323 steps, 0 failed. The watchdog stopped the `ui build (--no-run)` step after 15 minutes with no output (slow box). I built the UI tests with cargo. Then I ran `--only "ui suites"` again: 9 steps, 0 failed (lib, boundary, boundary_picks, contour_dxf_sketch, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_example, theme_files, waterjet_tool).
- The quick plan included `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `catalog_groove_part_off`, `post_not_judged` and `waterjet_profile`. All passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base f2aa981b5`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- After the clippy fix (`.expect_err` in two tests), `waterjet_profile` ran again: 13 passed.

## Review fix verification (2026-11-24)

The review requested screenshots only. The PR head stays `92c452b54089449b281adff1f81c88d8776607ed`.
No source change or new pin was needed. The worktree is clean.

The three existing UI pins failed with the parent waterjet page. All three passed after restoration:
- `waterjet_compensation_uses_a_plain_control_label`
- `waterjet_tab_position_rows_have_unique_names`
- `waterjet_zero_lead_in_names_the_part_edge_pierce`

Commands on this final head:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **RED**, 332 steps; 331 passed after build-cache recovery. The UI lib step failed. It reported 1,581 passed, seven failed, and eight ignored. All seven failures report the unavailable graphics adapter. The 13 waterjet tests and eight UI integration suites passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **GREEN**.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: **RED**, 103 steps; one unexpected failure, zero stalls, 32.3 minutes. Five registered expected failures were accepted by the gate.
- Heavy failure: `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`, at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:157`. The path counts were `(4688, 4660, 1980)`. This review round changes no code. No change to that test is in scope.
- `app suites: example_catalog`: 39 passed, four ignored in quick. Its heavy step also passed.
- `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`: one passed each.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test golden_cl`: 34 passed, including the waterjet golden.

Both gates started with `upstream/main` at `9adabbb84ce8ae89decbf5453270bacc139f9efd`.
Another process advanced that shared ref to `8be002085c989c4399a243dbd535865effa054ef` during heavy.
The merge-base stayed `f2aa981b51a3453428fb294c6c71c575a0178ef6`, so the selected diff stayed the same.
The gates did not trial-merge that later main. No hardware GPU run was possible on this host.
The failed steps are recorded here. No unrelated repair was made.

## Goldens moved

None. The quick plan ran the example catalog suites, and they passed. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed. The waterjet path notes changed text. No golden records these notes.

title: perf(playback): cut the twin-able ops into a dense layer (#2629 S3b)
body:
## What changed

This PR is slice S3b of #2629: the playback worker side. It stacks on nothing; S3a (#3878) is on main.

The playback gets an opt-in **layer mode** (`PlayWorker::spawn_layered(seed, cutter)`):

- Before the first cut, each op gets one owner. A plain op goes to the layer when its tool is a ball or a flat end mill and its moves are linear and upright. A plain op has no rotary, turning, undercut or drill. The f64 field cuts every other op, and never a layer op.
- `camcraft_sim::stock_sim::LayerPlay` keeps the layer: a dense f32 cut layer on the lattice of the packed frame. Its value at move k is the max-law fold of the layer moves before k. It has its own keyframes (every stride, 256 MiB budget), and it cuts only when a frame is published.
- A cutter from the caller (`LayerCutter`) cuts each batch onto the layer. `cpu_layer_cutter` is the CPU twin law (`run_twin_items_onto`, bit-exact to the one-batch twin). In S3c the UI gives a GPU cutter on its render device.
- A frame is `max(pack_cut(field), layer)` and is always a whole layer (`stock_play_worker_frame.rs`).
- A layer fault (a cutter error, or a window over the twin ceiling) turns the mode off. The reason is logged. The field is then rebuilt from the uncut stock with every op, at the same position.

No caller turns the mode on in this PR, so the product picture does not change. `camcraft-app` gets no `camcraft-gpu` dependency. The worker never makes a second `wgpu` instance (#3589), and it does not use the software shared device (review of PR #3532).

Review notes of PR #3878 that belong to S3b:
- **The spot-check tie** (`crates/gpu/src/cut_run.rs` `want_at`): the bound now takes the largest claim margin of each item whose CPU value is within its own margin of the result. Before, a base value that won gave a bound of about one ULP. A spring pass over a keyframe could then refuse a good GPU layer and turn the GPU path off for the process.
- **The device-loss `Err` of `cut_into`** is now asserted in `a_lost_device_takes_the_cpu_law_and_never_crashes`.

Moves for the 400-line law: `FieldPlay::cut` moves without a change (off mode) to `crates/app/src/stock_play_cut.rs` (`stock_play.rs` 430 -> 409 lines). The frame packing moves to `crates/app/src/stock_play_worker_frame.rs` (`stock_play_worker.rs` 406 -> 359 lines).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/stock_play_picture.rs`:
  - `the_layer_playback_draws_the_field_picture_within_the_twin_margin`: the layered worker and the field worker play the same positions, with a half-drawn move, the end, and a backward seek. At each landed frame, the drawn layer `max(mesh, cut)` of the layer worker is within the twin margin of the field worker. It never draws more removal than the field (1e-6). Each layer frame is whole.
  - `a_layer_fault_falls_back_to_the_field_picture_bit_for_bit`: a cutter that faults at once, or after two batches (a lost GPU device). The mode goes off, and the rebuilt field is bit-equal to the field playback at the same position.
  - `the_layer_mode_is_set_once_before_the_first_cut`.
- `crates/sim/tests/stock_cut_twin.rs`:
  - `the_layer_playback_is_the_one_batch_twin_at_every_seek`: forward, jump, backward and end seeks, bit-equal to the one-batch twin.
  - `the_layer_frame_shows_the_travelled_part_of_the_move_in_flight`.
  - `an_op_without_a_twin_stays_on_the_field_by_name`, `a_bad_base_layer_is_refused_by_name`.
  - The existing `the_gpu_kernel_fixtures_match_the_twin` stays green after the `run_twin` refactor.
- `crates/gpu/tests/cut_onto.rs`: `a_tie_with_the_keyframe_does_not_refuse_a_good_gpu_layer` (new), and the `cut_into` lost-device assert.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6) on 5522dfe96: green, 94 steps, 0 failed. The steps were the app, gpu and sim lib tests, every `app:stock_play*` suite, and the app and sim suites that the `sim::stock_sim` gate map reaches.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui`: clean (the UI keeps `PlayWorker::spawn`).
- Heavy lanes: none (a P2 PR gets no heavy step).

## Not exercised

- A GPU cutter: no `LayerCutter` calls `camcraft-gpu` in this slice (S3c).
- The UI: nothing calls `spawn_layered`. In the layer mode `FieldView::stock` does not hold the layer ops' cut. So the CPU eye (`cpu_eye.rs` `march_job`) must not get a layered worker. S3c turns the mode on only with the trace eye.
- A hardware adapter.

## What remains of #2629 (S3c)

- The GPU cutter: map `TwinItem` to `camcraft_gpu::CutItem`, then call `cut_onto_or_cpu_on` (or `cut_into`) on the render device, off the UI thread.
- The UI turns the layer mode on only with the trace eye.
- Patch frames for the layer.
- The path choice from hardware timings.
- The parity proof on a hardware adapter.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2629-gpu-playback-layer.md`.

Effort: max.

Changelog: none (an opt-in mode that no caller turns on yet)

Refs #2629

title: perf(gpu): cut the stock onto a keyframe layer on the GPU (#2629 S3a)
body:
## What changed

This PR is slice S3a of #2629. The issue is too large for one PR (see the escalation comment of 2026-11-22). The S2 kernel cut only from the empty floor. A playback could therefore not continue from a keyframe on the GPU. This slice adds the incremental start in `camcraft-gpu`:

- `crates/gpu/src/cut.wgsl`: a new entry point `cs_encode`. It turns a layer (the f32 bits that `cs_decode` writes) back into order-preserving keys, in place.
- `CutKernel::cut_into`: cuts a batch into a buffer of the caller (encode, cut, decode). It reads nothing back. S3c uses it on the `Scene.cut` buffer of the render device.
- `CutKernel::run_onto`: the same cut on its own buffer, read back.
- `cut_cpu_onto`: the CPU law of the same cut. With the max law it is bit-exact to the one-batch cut.
- `cut_onto_or_cpu` and `cut_onto_or_cpu_on`: the run-time choice of `cut_or_cpu`. These conditions give the CPU law, with the reason, logged one time:
  - `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`;
  - no adapter, or no compute;
  - a lost device, or a kernel error;
  - a failed spot check (`spot_check_onto`).
- A base layer with the wrong texel count or a non-finite value is refused by name.
- `cut_gpu.rs` is split along the buffer seam into `cut_buf.rs` (the 400-line law). The code that moved is not changed, except that `first += ITEMS_PER_DISPATCH` is now a saturating add.

Display only. The verdict (`simulate_document`) and the post gate do not change.

## Pinning tests (`crates/gpu/tests/cut_onto.rs`)

1. `the_gpu_cut_onto_a_keyframe_matches_the_cpu_law_or_skips_by_name`: GPU against CPU on a small fixture (ball, tilted flat, level flat), within `SPOT_MARGIN_FRACTION` of the claim margin. It also checks that `cut_into` equals `run_onto` bit for bit, and that a short target buffer is refused. When there is no adapter, the test prints a named SKIP. With `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` it fails. Reading on this machine: `"Microsoft Basic Render Driver" via Dx12`, max |GPU - CPU law| = 0.
2. `the_off_switch_takes_the_cpu_law_by_name`: a child process with `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` gets `CutPath::Cpu` with a reason that names the switch, and the CPU bits.
3. `a_lost_device_takes_the_cpu_law_and_never_crashes`: a child process destroys the shared device (the real device-lost callback). Then `run_onto` gives an `Err`, `cut_into` does not panic, and the two fallback entries give the CPU bits. The shared path names the loss.

Also: `the_incremental_cpu_law_is_the_one_batch_cut_bit_for_bit`, `a_bad_base_layer_is_refused_by_name`, and the unit test `a_layer_uploads_as_its_little_endian_bits`.

New top-level test file: `camcraft-gpu` has no directory suite. This binary must touch only the one shared `wgpu` instance of its process (#3589). It runs the switch and device-loss cases as child processes of itself. `cut_parity.rs` is at 378 lines.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6): green. The steps were gpu lib, gpu:cut_onto and gpu:cut_parity.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-gpu`: all suites green.
- `camcraft-ui` lib tests: 1587 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored (`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`).
- Heavy lanes: none (a P2 PR gets no heavy step).

## Not exercised

- A hardware adapter. The GPU parity ran on the WARP software adapter only. Precondition 1 of the S2 review (parity on a hardware adapter) is still open.
- No viewport code changes in this slice, so there are no screenshots.

## What remains of #2629

- S3b: the worker protocol in `camcraft-app`. On the GPU path, the worker sends the twin work for each frame. It keeps CPU checkpoints for the fallback and for the operations that the twin refuses.
- S3c: the UI side in `crates/ui/src/trace/`. It dispatches `cut_into` off the UI thread on the render device. It keeps the keyframe store in a VRAM budget, and it falls back to the CPU frames on any error.
- The path choice by batch size and adapter kind, from hardware timings.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2629-gpu-cut-onto.md`.

Effort: max (the issue was escalated from effort:high before this run).

Changelog: none (internal kernel entries; the viewport does not use them yet)

Refs #2629

title: fix(2d): refuse a Face whose 'Do not touch' keep-out blocks a level
body:
## What changed
- A Face operation with "Do not touch" items is now refused when the keep-out blocks a facing level.
- The refusal names the protected items, Cut Z and the depth that the face can reach.
- The refusal tells the user what to do: set Cut Z to the reached depth, use a smaller clearance, or remove the item.
- The old note "blocked N facing level(s); the remaining levels stayed clear" is removed. It can no longer occur.
- `face_keep::Tally` records the lowest level that is cut and the lowest level that is asked for.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/3526-face-keep-depth.md`.

## Cause
- The keep-out of a level covers the heights from that level up to the clearance plane.
- Thus a lower level gets the same keep-out or a larger one, and the blocked levels are always the lowest levels.
- When a lower level was blocked, the Face generated anyway. The face stopped above Cut Z everywhere.
- Only a note said so. Nothing marked the operation, and the post was not blocked.

## Why a refusal
- A `Toolpath` has no "incomplete" state. It has notes only, and the app and the post read no note as a state.
- An "incomplete" state is a change to the cache, the project file, the status line and the post gate. That is too large for this defect.
- The issue permits a refusal. A refusal is visible and blocks the post.
- The workaround is direct: Cut Z at the reached depth faces clean.

## Tests
- Pin: `face_keep::a_keepout_that_blocks_the_lower_levels_refuses_with_the_depth_reached` (crates/motion/tests/face_keep.rs).
  - The keep-out changes with Z: a 12 mm box above Z -1.5, and the whole face below it. Levels are Z -1 and Z -2 (Cut Z).
  - The test asserts the refusal, the item name, "Cut Z -2.000" and "Z -1.000".
- Pin proof (mutation): with `face_keep.rs` from upstream/main, the pin FAILS. The face generated at Z -1 only, with the note "blocked 1 facing level(s)". With the fix, the pin PASSES.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 07b9d2f9b: green, 25 steps, 0 failed. This includes motion `face_keep`, `face_holes`, `face_blend`, `top_z_level`, and app `do_not_touch_face`, `example_catalog`, `solid_law_goldens`, `first_part_programs`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on head 07b9d2f9b: the plan has 101 steps (motion heavy and app heavy). The run stopped at the 2-hour tool limit during step 80.
  - Steps 1-79: 78 ok, 1 failed.
  - The failure: `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`, "the mesh behind the Linux path pin", left 5232, right 6228.
  - This count is the imported mesh. It is read before any toolpath is made, so a Face change cannot move it. Open issue #3085 tracks this count band.
  - Steps 80-101 (app heavy, after `rotary_field_parity`) did not run.

## Goldens moved
- None. The quick gate ran `example_catalog`, `solid_law_goldens` and `first_part_programs` on the final head, and all passed with no change.

## Not exercised
- An app-level test with a real model that is wider below the face. The motion pin uses a Z-dependent keep-out closure. This is the same input that the app gives to `face_over_kept`.
- Heavy steps 80-101 (see above).

title: fix(2d): warn on a selected Helix, Ramp or Plunge start-side entry; retire the dead-end ramp
body:
## What changed

The maintainer's rule on #3748: Helix, Ramp and Plunge stay lead-in types. Arc in the cut plane (the #3746 entry from the air) is the recommended entry for "Pass starts at" Inside and Outside. A non-recommended choice gives a warning.

- `sim::verify`: new advisory `Warning::EntryNotRecommended { at, entry, inside }` and the one sentence `entry_advice` (selected type, recommended Arc, reason). The warning does not hold the post. MCP kind: `entry_not_recommended`.
- `motion`: where the Arc entry from the air applies (the air room exists) and the user selected Inside or Outside with Helix, Ramp or Plunge, the ladder (`pocket.rs`, `pocket_avoid.rs`) writes one `entry:` note. The entry runs as selected. Auto and an Adaptive op get no advice.
- `app`: `operation::entry_not_recommended` turns the note into the one warning. The status line counts it.
- `ui`: the Lead in / Lead out page of 2D Offset greys nothing out. With Inside or Outside and Helix, Ramp or Plunge, it shows the same sentence as a visible line under the Type selector.
- Removed the automatic #3577 dead-end ramp: `level_ramp_entry.rs` (`dead_end_ramp`, `too_short_at`, `stand_in_note`), the `ramp_starts` marks and plumbing, and `StartSide::ramp_fallback_note`.

What was left of the automatic ramp on `main` (ed6f980ef): #3744 had already stopped the marks round a part, and #3790 stopped the #3567 dead ends there. The ramp was still live for the pocket form of Outside (`!around_part`, no stock known). A later pass there now takes the pass link's entry, which is the user's (#2265 restart). #3746's named stand-in for a selected Arc (a helix, then a ramp, each named) stays.

**Overlap:** this PR touches `ladder_links.rs::pass_link`. It deletes only the `dead_end_ramp` call block (old lines 187-195). The #3837 Clearance arm is kept (origin/main merged, no conflict).

## Pinning tests

- `motion` `pass_start_engagement`: `a_selected_entry_is_kept_and_named_once` (pin 1), `the_arc_entry_has_no_helix_or_ramp_and_no_advice` (pin 2), `start_side_pass_has_no_automatic_ramp` (pin 3), `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` (no ramp exemption, round a part), `a_short_dead_end_no_longer_falls_back_to_auto`.
- `app` `offset_pass_start`: `entry_advice::the_advice_note_posts_one_advisory_warning`; heavy `entry_advice::fig8_outside_selected_helix_warns_once_and_arc_not_at_all`.
- `ui` lib: `the_leads_tab_advises_arc_next_to_the_entry_type_for_inside_and_outside` (pin 4; the Type combo is not disabled; the `#[test]` count of camcraft-ui goes up by one).
- `sim` lib: `the_advice_names_the_selected_and_the_recommended_type`.

Red first: pins 1 and 4 and the app and sim pins use the new advice API and the new warning, so they cannot pass on `main`. Pins 2 and 3 round a part were not run on `main`; #3744 and #3746 can already make them green there.

## Readings

- Quick gate `--base origin/main` (384 steps, 55.6 min): 1 failed, `app:adaptive_pass_start` (an Adaptive op on its ring fallback got the advice). Fixed in abfaf7884; the suite then passed (4 of 4). The other 383 steps passed on the head before that fix.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the final head.
- Heavy: `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: offset_pass_start"` on the final head: ok, 7 passed (known-fail #3825 skipped by the gate).

## Not exercised

- The full quick gate was not run again after abfaf7884 (one condition in two files).
- The light lane and other heavy lanes.
- No app window was opened.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/3748-entry-warnings.md`. The 2D Offset seed stays Helix; follow-up #3843 owns an Arc default for Inside and Outside.

Changelog: 2D Offset "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside: a selected Helix, Ramp or Plunge lead-in is kept and gives one warning that recommends Arc (also shown on the Lead in / Lead out page); the automatic dead-end ramp is removed.

Effort: high

title: feat(app): operation-level picks for toolpath start and exit positions
body:
Process change: yes

### Summary of Changes

Move toolpath start and exit picks from `links.approach` to operation-level `PathPicks` across `OpParams`.

- **Operation-level storage:** Store `picks: PathPicks` directly on each operation parameter variant (`OpParams::*`). `PathPicks` holds `start: Vec<PathPick>` and `exit: Vec<PathPick>`.
- **Project format migration:** Load legacy `.camproj` files with `start_point` and `exit_point` under `links.approach`, or legacy `WireContour` with `start` coordinates, and migrate them to the operation-level `picks` field. In `OperationDto`, support both `"src"` and `"source"`.
- **Digest and caching:** Stamp operation picks in `OpParams::stamp_picks` with distinct markers (`0xC7` for start, `0xC8` for exit), preserving legacy digests when picks are empty.
- **MCP surface:** Expose `picks` with `start` and `exit` points in MCP operation edit and add commands, validating against pick capabilities per operation type. Updated `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`.
- **Decision document:** Added `docs/decisions/3339-operation-level-picks.md`.

- `cargo check --workspace` passed across all crates.

- `cargo test --manifest-path crates/app/Cargo.toml --test start_exit_shared` passed (4/4 tests).

### What Was Not Exercised

- Multi-point pick chains (single pick per role supported in this stage).

Changelog: Toolpath start and exit points now store as operation-level picks across all operation types.

title: fix(motion): apply stock to leave axially and radially in 3D Pocket
body:
### Summary of Changes

The 3D Pocket roughing ladder now applies `stock_to_leave` in both radial and axial directions.

- **Level target query:** In `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`, query `level_target(facets, footprint, z - axial_leave)` instead of plane `z`. This keeps tool radius plus stock allowance XY distance from material overhead, so top faces and shallow slopes keep their allowance.
- **Flat floor detection:** In `crates/motion/src/machining3d/floor_levels.rs`, when `stock_to_leave > 0.0`, search for horizontal upward faces across `[bottom_z, top_z)` and deduplicate levels within `1e-9` mm. This ensures deep floors receive a level at `floor + stock_to_leave`.
- **Catalog case update:** Regenerated catalog case `3d/rough-finish` using `cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rough-finish`.
- **Decision document:** Added `docs/decisions/3669-3d-pocket-stock-to-leave.md`.

### Readings and Verification

- Passed all 4 integration tests in `crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_stock_to_leave.rs`:
  - `through_pocket_without_floor_cuts_to_bottom_z_and_keeps_wall_allowance`
  - `flat_top_boss_and_floor_both_keep_axial_allowance`
  - `rough_finish_dome_and_plate_keep_axial_and_radial_allowance`

- `cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rough-finish` completed cleanly.

### What Was Not Exercised

- Multi-axis rotary continuous toolpaths (`pocket3d_air_split` preserves existing behavior with `axial_leave = 0.0`).

Changelog: 3D Pocket roughing now keeps the stock allowance axially on tops, shallow slopes, and floors as well as radially.

title: fix(2d): peck a contour dive deeper than one stepdown below the cut floor
body:
## What changed

A contour dive below its ring's first level pecks when it would cut more than one stepdown below the cleared floor. This applies to dives past tabs and wall-side graze dives, including tabbed bore entries.

Each peck feeds one stepdown, retracts above the material, and returns above the last depth before the next feed. One note describes the pecked entry. The uncut floor is the material top, or one stepdown above a lower ring's first level. The first level never pecks.

The floor check now proves coverage of the entire tool disc. An exact matching endpoint or plunge column proves coverage. An axis-aligned straight feed also proves coverage when the target centre lies on its centreline. Uncertain coverage counts as uncut material. The proof does not use finite samples or approximate arc chords.

The old 4,096-peck cap no longer permits a long final cut. Every required stepdown is retained within the existing contour depth limit.

The XY path, tab layout, leads, and level order stay the same.

## Cause

The levels above cut the lead-in start of a tab window only at the ring start. Other windows can start above a 2.5 mm crescent of uncut material. The original dive cut 18 mm below that floor. The stay-down ramp preset cut 13.5 mm at window 0.

The review also found an uncovered rim with a 0.002 mm perpendicular lead. The shortened sample radius missed it. The peck cap could append a 9.04 mm final cut for a 0.01 mm stepdown.

## Pins and mutation proof

The L-shape fixture is in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs`. Its independent oracle now samples the actual tool radius and counts straight plunge columns. It measures circular sweeps analytically. Inscribed chords create artificial gaps at the full rim, so they no longer stand in for earlier flat arcs. The safety assertions stay the same.

- `no_contour_descent_goes_more_than_one_stepdown_below_the_disc_floor` checks all descents of four entry presets.
- `a_short_perpendicular_lead_pecks_below_the_uncut_rim` checks the public generator with a 0.002 mm lead and a 0.0001 mm tolerance.
- `an_offset_column_leaves_an_uncut_rim` checks a prior column that misses the actual rim.
- `an_offset_straight_cut_does_not_prove_full_disc_coverage` checks an offset straight sweep and a proven centreline case.
- `a_dive_beyond_4096_pecks_preserves_every_stepdown` checks all 5,000 depths down to Z-50 at a 0.01 mm stepdown.
- `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program` checks the shipped router NC file through the CLI. Before regeneration, `first_part_programs` had one pass and one failure: the router NC pin was red.

The window readings use `(depth below floor, crescent)`. Plunge windows 1 to 3 change from `(18.0, 2.5)` to `(4.5, 2.5)`. The stay-down window 0 changes from `(13.5, 2.5)` to `(4.5, 2.5)`. Lead None remains `(2.7, 0.0)`.

Mutation proof:

- Restoring the old sampler makes `an_offset_column_leaves_an_uncut_rim` and `an_offset_straight_cut_does_not_prove_full_disc_coverage` fail. The public pin `a_short_perpendicular_lead_pecks_below_the_uncut_rim` also fails: at `(10.152613, -3.002)`, the floor is Z0 and the dive reaches Z-18. Restoring the fix passes all five peck unit tests and all five public contour tests.
- Restoring the old cap makes `a_dive_beyond_4096_pecks_preserves_every_stepdown` fail: it returns 4,097 depths instead of 5,000. Restoring the fix passes that pin.
- Restoring the literal router NC file from reviewed head `3d1564e10` makes `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program` fail. Restoring the final NC file passes that exact pin. The restored file matches its saved byte hash. Both `first_part_programs` tests also pass.

The final gates below cover the refreshed head. After the fixture corrections, restoring the old sampled coverage also makes `machining2d::tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor` fail: zero pecks instead of four. Restoring the fix passes that pin.

## Final validation

Final head: `250592fb756370115d7472412d6fe5a2c1de07d5`. Tested base: `6d0381f1977b267885e22b3ddf55950b098fd319`, fetched before the final gates. The worktree is clean. Upstream advanced after the gates started. A read-only `git merge-tree` check confirms that the final head merges cleanly with latest upstream `1e182f2cf8b55995965d2b19e99b2647afddcde4`. This check required no hand resolution. The gates do not include those newer upstream commits.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `03d84130a9a139914e40e1a6ec8a5114d29ecc83`: 173 steps; 171 passed, 2 failed, 0 stalled, in 64.6 minutes. The two failures identified stale expectations below. On the final head, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --failed gate-logs/quick-20261124-121421` passes both corrected steps: 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 stalled (`machining2d` and `first_router_part`).
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED: 104 actual steps; 103 passed, one failed, zero stalled, in 84.0 minutes. The release build passed in 1,312 seconds. The plan listed 103 steps; an existing probe expanded it to 104. Seven lanes are outside the diff reach. The failure is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. At `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:79`, the mesh has 5,232 triangles; the pin expects 6,228. It fails before path generation. This mesh pin is outside the latest review findings and was not changed. Read-only diffs against tested base `6d0381f1977b267885e22b3ddf55950b098fd319` are empty for the test, STEP fixture, import chain, STEP meshing code, manifests, and lock file. These checks establish unchanged inputs; they do not reproduce the failure on the baseline. No baseline reproduction was run. The full heavy gate is red.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on the final head in 5 minutes 16 seconds.
- `app suites: example_catalog` in the full quick gate: 41 passed, 4 ignored, in 44.81 seconds. A final-head run during the release build hit the 60-second limits for two 3D rough-finish cases. The isolated final-head retry passed all 41 tests, with four ignored, in 107.94 seconds. The rough-finish rebuild took 29.764 seconds; regeneration took 29.558 seconds.
- Final-head small suites: 49 passed. Counts: `example_catalog_adaptive` 1, `example_catalog_edge_work` 1, `first_part_programs` 2, `first_router_part` 4, `golden_cl` 34, and `solid_law_goldens` 7. Command: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-app --no-fail-fast --test example_catalog_adaptive --test example_catalog_edge_work --test first_router_part --test first_part_programs --test golden_cl --test solid_law_goldens -- --test-threads=1`.
- Router suites: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test first_router_part --test first_part_programs -- --test-threads=1` passes all six tests. This ran before the final commit on identical source and fixture contents.
- Final-head motion pins: all five peck unit tests and all five `contour_tab_entry` tests passed. Commands: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-motion --lib contour_peck::tests:: -- --test-threads=1` and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-motion --test contour_tab_entry -- --test-threads=1`.
- Merged tested base `6d0381f1977b267885e22b3ddf55950b098fd319` after #3833 merged during this fix round. The only hand-resolved conflict was the import of `contour_peck` and `wall_ramp`. Both imports remain. No logic conflicted, and both safety guards remain.

## Goldens moved

The program changes add pecked tab-window dives. Each program was regenerated with the repository tool. The full quick gate found two stale expectations:

- `machining2d::tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor` counted intermediate pecks as entries. The correction keeps six entries and counts four bottom dives and four pecks separately.
- `first_router_part` found a stale cached project. Conservative coverage adds two pecks, at Z-4 and Z-8, before the first bottom-window dive at `(176, 80.991)`.

- `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.nc`: generated with `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/contour-tabs`. Three dives now feed through Z4, Z2, and Z0, with retracts between pecks. The original change adds 18 lines. This fix round makes no further change to this golden.
- `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.camproj`: the cached path contains the same moves. The project save updates its version from 77 to 78.
- `examples/first-router-part.camproj`: generated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` and `first_router_part`. The tab-window dives now peck through Z-4, Z-8, and Z-12. The note is added. Final regeneration also updates the initial bottom window at `(176, 80.991)`. The exact regeneration hook, `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test first_router_part first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal -- --exact --test-threads=1`, passes. The project correction adds 82 lines and removes one relative to the first refreshed head.
- `examples/first-router-part.nc`: regenerated with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- process examples/first-router-part.camproj -o examples/first-router-part.nc` (exit 0). Three direct dives now peck through Z-4, Z-8, and Z-12. The initial regeneration added 18 lines. Regeneration of the updated cached project adds the first bottom-window pecks as well. The final diff adds 24 lines relative to the reviewed head `3d1564e10`: 18 for the three later windows and six for the initial bottom window at `(176, 80.991)`.

`contour_tabs_case_posts_the_lead_moves_and_the_tab_lifts` counts peck retracts separately from lead-out lifts: six of each. The case README states this distinction.

## Not exercised

Windows and macOS were not built. The light tier was not run separately. The heavy gate excludes seven lanes that the diff does not reach. This PR changes no UI; screenshots do not apply.

The lead-in arc after a tab window still feeds through the 2.5 mm crescent at the target level. This issue addresses the plunge only.

## Overlaps and decision

- #3834 also touches `contour.rs`, `contour_step.rs`, and the `Step` constructor. The second PR to merge needs a refresh.
- #3833 is incorporated through the merge of the tested base.

`docs/decisions/3678-tab-window-dive.md` records the peck, conservative coverage proof, and removal of the unsafe peck cap. Cutting the window lead-ins on earlier levels was dropped because it changes the XY travel.

Effort: high

Changelog: 2D Contour: a dive past a tab (and the stay-down entry of a tabbed level) that goes more than one stepdown below the floor the levels above cut now pecks one stepdown at a time, with a note.

Fixes #3678

title: fix(app): warn when a 2D Pocket tool cannot fit, refuse a too-narrow Slot edit
body:
## What changed

- A new advice, `operation::pocket_fit_advice`, says when a 2D Pocket's tool has no position in its region. It builds the region the way Generate builds it: `collect_job`, `region_for_job`, then the area controls (`apply_area_full`). It applies the generator's own test. That test is now public as `machining2d::pocket_tool_fits` (the `non_sliver_center(region, r + stock_to_leave)` test of `pocket_started_on`).
- The advice does not run when it cannot build the same region: a refused collect, a tilted frame, a rotated WCS, a sketch source, rest machining, or the retired Adaptive strategy.
- The MCP replies of `add_operation`, `edit_operation`, `set_tool` and `set_operation_area` carry the sentence in `warning`. This follows the `clearance_warning` pattern. When the clearance warning also applies, the two sentences are joined with "; ".
- `EditOperationParams` refuses a plain Slot edit that changes `width` or `stock_to_leave` and leaves the mounted tool too wide. It uses the #3475 door (`slot_gate`) and its sentence. An edit of other fields does not run this check, so an older document stays editable.

## Cause

#3475 refused a too-wide Slot tool at create, at `set_tool` and at `ChangeTool`. It did not refuse a Slot width edit. It added no Pocket check, because only the generator's region can say if a pocket fits.

## Tests

Pins (all in the `mcp` directory suite of `camcraft-app`):

- `pocket_tool_fit::a_tool_wider_than_a_closed_inside_pocket_is_warned_and_the_generator_agrees`: a 10 mm tool on an 8 x 8 mm stock pocket. `set_tool`, `set_operation_area` (Inside) and `edit_operation` give the warning. `generate` refuses with "narrower than the tool".
- `pocket_tool_fit::an_outside_pocket_that_the_generator_cuts_has_no_warning`: the same pocket with Outside containment. No warning, and `generate` gives status `ok`.
- `slot_tool_fit::edit_operation_refuses_a_slot_width_below_the_tool_without_mutation`: a width edit to 4 mm under a 6 mm tool is refused with the #3475 sentence. A `stock_to_leave` edit to 0.5 mm is refused. `get_job` does not change. A feed edit passes.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pin run, code restored):

- `crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs` from upstream/main: the Slot pin fails. Restored: passes.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` and `mcp/area.rs` from upstream/main: the Inside pocket pin fails. Restored: passes.
- The advice without the area controls (an estimate on the raw region): the Outside pin fails. Restored: passes.

Gate (final head):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: see the result below.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: see the result below.

Results:

- Quick gate plan: 452 steps (the `motion` change reaches each app suite). The first run stopped at a background time limit in step 270. Steps 270-445 and 446-452 then ran with `--only` on the same head. Result: 451 steps ok, 1 failed. The one failed step is `motion suites: pass_start_levels` (`pocket_outside::adaptive_spiral_round_a_part_outside_equals_main_before_3818`). It also fails with `crates/motion` set back to upstream/main, so this PR does not cause it. It is filed as #3853.
- The suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work` ran in the quick plan: ok.
- clippy: clean (no warnings).
- The pins: 5 of 5 ok (`cargo xtask gate test tool_fit --crate camcraft-app --binary mcp`).
- After the gate, one docs-only amend added the #3859 reference to the decision file. No code changed.

## Goldens moved

None. The change adds a warning field and one refusal. It does not change a generator, a posted program or a recorded `.cl`/`.nc` file. `example_catalog*` ran in the quick gate (see above).

## Not exercised

- The UI operation page does not show the warning yet. The UI advice must be cached by the frame-cost rule. This is #3859.
- Tilted frames, rotated WCS, sketch sources and rest machining: the advice does not run for them, by design.
- No heavy lane. This is a `P3` PR.

## Overlaps

- #3251 touches `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`, in `patched` / `opt_in_kept`. This PR changes `clearance_warning` and `set_tool`. Different functions; whichever merges second refreshes.

## Pre-existing red test

`pass_start_levels::pocket_outside::adaptive_spiral_round_a_part_outside_equals_main_before_3818` (motion) fails on this machine. It also fails with `crates/motion` set back to upstream/main. Filed as #3853.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket now warns at edit time (MCP `warning`) when its tool has no position in the region that Generate cuts; a Slot width or stock-to-leave edit that leaves the tool too wide is refused.

Fixes #3631

title: feat(cli): camcraft-cli --ui sends MCP tool calls to the running window
body:
## What changed (part 1 of #3751: the `--ui` transport)

- Each CamCraft window opens a UI link at start (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_window.rs`). `CAMCRAFT_UI_LINK=off` starts a window without it.
  - Linux and macOS: a Unix domain socket in the user's link folder (folder 0700, socket 0600).
  - Windows: TCP on `127.0.0.1` only, with a port that the OS selects. std has no named pipe. The dependency question for a named pipe is on #3751.
- The window writes a discovery file `<pid>.json` (pid, transport, address, token, open project, version) and removes it when it closes (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs`). The file follows the open project.
- Each connection must send the token from the file first. Any other first line closes the connection before a line reaches the app.
- The session speaks the MCP JSON-RPC of `camcraft-cli mcp`. The window answers each line in `mcp_host::pump` with `answer_live_with`, as for `--mcp-port`: on the UI thread, on the window's History, behind the same live gate. There is no second command set. Ctrl+Z undoes a CLI step.
- New CLI lane `camcraft-cli --ui [--window <pid|project>] <verb>` (`crates/app/src/cli_ui.rs`, client in `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs`):
  - `call <tool> [<json-args>]`: one tool call; prints the tool's JSON; a refused tool exits 1.
  - `mcp`: a stdio MCP bridge to the window.
  - `windows`: lists the link files.
- No window: a clear error ("no running CamCraft window ... (nothing ran)") and exit 3. The CLI never falls back to a headless document. Several windows without `--window`: a list and exit 2.
- The listener of `--mcp-port` now serves a stream type that hides TCP or Unix (`crates/app/src/mcp/wire.rs`). `port_from` moved to `port_flag.rs` (400-line law). The behaviour of `--mcp-port` does not change.
- No new dependency. The token comes from std's `RandomState` keys (seeded from the OS random source).

Decision file: `docs/decisions/3751-cli-ui-link.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::ui_link::a_cli_ui_call_shows_in_the_window_and_ctrl_z_removes_it` (camcraft-ui lib): the harness window opens its link; the `--ui` lane (`cli_ui::run_in`) sends `set_stock`, `add_tool`, `add_operation`; the browser shows `Face1`; Ctrl+Z removes it; a refused call exits 1; the link file goes with the window.
- `mcp_live` / `ui_link::a_cli_call_with_no_window_says_so_and_exits_3`: the real `camcraft-cli` binary with an empty link folder, a stale file, and an unknown pid: exit 3, the message, nothing on stdout.
- `mcp_live` / `ui_link::a_wrong_token_is_refused_and_the_window_goes_on_serving`: a wrong token is refused (exit code 1), no line reaches the app, and the next client with the right token is served.
- `mcp_live` / `ui_link::bad_ui_arguments_are_usage_errors`, `the_link_file_follows_the_open_project`, `the_link_folder_is_the_users_own`.
- `cli` / `every_subcommand_answers_help_and_names_its_flags` now walks the `--ui` lane too (`HELP_LANES`).

## Readings

- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6): 185 steps, 0 failed (`mcp_live` 19 passed, `cli` 13 passed, camcraft-ui lib 1584 passed).
- Clippy `-D warnings`: camcraft-app (lib, bins, `mcp_live`, `cli`), camcraft-ui (lib, bins, lib tests).

## Not exercised

- The Unix socket arms (`#[cfg(unix)]`) were not compiled or run here: the work was on Windows. The post-merge runner (Linux) builds them.
- No real window was started on the desktop. The UI test uses the harness only.
- `--ui mcp` (the stdio bridge) has no test of its own; it uses the same `connect` as `--ui call`.
- `script` and `process` do not take `--ui`. Follow-up: #3850.
- Part 2 (`--skill <target> install`) is not in this PR.

Changelog: `camcraft-cli --ui [--window <pid|project>] call <tool> [<json>]` (and `--ui mcp`, `--ui windows`) sends MCP tool calls to a running CamCraft window, which runs them on its own undo history; with no window it exits 3 and runs nothing.

Effort: max

title: fix(mcp): run a stdio generate on a worker thread and honour cancel
body:
## What changed
- `camcraft-cli mcp` (the stdio server) runs a `generate` call on a worker thread. A new module, `crates/app/src/mcp/background.rs`, holds the lane.
- A reader thread moves the input lines through a channel with capacity one. The session thread keeps the world.
- The session stages each operation on its own thread (`StagedGeneration`, #2257). A worker thread runs the pure finish.
- Other calls answer while the worker runs, for example `get_job` and `save_project`. The generate answer goes out when its result lands. Answers can come out of request order. JSON-RPC permits this.
- A result lands through the History only if `still_current` is true. If the operation or its cached path changed during the run, the call is refused by name. The GUI worker uses the same rule.
- `notifications/cancelled` with the generate's `requestId` drops the generate result. The cancelled worker keeps its slot until it finishes. No answer goes out for that id.
- A second `generate` while one runs is refused by name, including after cancellation until its worker finishes. `open_project` is refused while a generate runs, because it replaces the world.
- At the end of input, a running generate still gets its answer.
- `script::api::generate_targets` is now shared by the script verb and the MCP lane, so the two paths run the same operations.
- The live GUI bridge and `Server::handle` stay synchronous.
- `cli.rs` gives `serve` a `BufReader` over `stdin()`, because the reader thread needs a `Send` handle.

## Cause
`mcp::serve` handled each line on one thread. `generate` ran the generator in the call, so the loop read no input until the generator ended. The protocol had no cancel path.

## Tests

The `mcp` directory suite includes the three original pins and four review pins.
The hidden `Server::hold_generations` hook holds a worker until the test releases it.
The final-head validation below records the commands, mutation proofs, and results.

## Goldens moved
None. The change does not touch a generator or a post. `example_catalog` ran in the quick gate and passed with no change.

## Heavy lanes
The final-head review round below records the full reached heavy run requested by the maintainer.

## Not exercised
- A generic blocking reader cannot be interrupted. After an output error, its owned thread can wait for input or EOF. It retains no session or world.
- The real `camcraft-cli mcp` binary over a pipe with a slow job. The QA project (mould core) is not on this machine. The pins drive `mcp::serve_with` in-process with the same loop.
- A real stop inside a generator. A cancelled worker runs to its end, and the session drops its result.
- The staging of a rest operation still simulates the operations ahead of it on the session thread. That part still blocks other calls.

## Still open on #3035
- The run time of Rough12, Rest6 and Waterline6 on the mould core.
- A cancel point inside the generators.

## Overlaps
None. No open PR changes `crates/app/src/mcp/mod.rs`, `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` or `crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3035-mcp-generate-worker.md`.


## Review fix round on c83ab4889bc8455306a74827b6c6f9a13e3ba308

The round addresses the four findings on head `91e412fdcb44ceee7a9d743b599c90cac24605c6`.

1. A cancelled worker retains the single worker slot until completion. Repeated retries receive the busy refusal.
   Pin: `background_generate::cancelled_workers_keep_the_worker_budget_until_they_finish`.
2. The event channel has capacity one. Input stops reading when the queue and pending line are full.
   Pin: `background_streams::blocked_output_bounds_the_input_queue`.
3. `name: null` takes the background path. Dispatch accepts the same non-null IDs as the synchronous handler.
   Pin: `background_generate::a_null_name_uses_the_background_lane_and_busy_guard`.
4. The input thread owns its reader. An output error returns without joining a blocked reader.
   Pin: `background_streams::an_output_error_returns_while_input_remains_open`.

### Pin proof

`CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 12 -p camcraft-app --test mcp background_ -- --test-threads=1` passed all seven background tests.

Each mutation failed its named pin. Restoring the fix passed the same pin:

- Drop the cancelled worker slot: the retry starts another held worker. RED, then GREEN.
- Increase the event channel capacity to 1,000: the reader consumes more than three lines while output blocks. RED, then GREEN.
- Remove null-name normalization: the held generate answers synchronously. RED, then GREEN.
- Restore the narrower ID dispatch: an accepted boolean ID bypasses the busy guard. RED, then GREEN.
- Join the input reader after an output error: `serve` does not return before input closes. RED, then GREEN.

The mutation checks ran before the commit. The final-head MCP suite runs the restored source.

### Final-head validation

Base: current `upstream/main`, `29488d99c9cdbe32b689f7c0d6d70d8361ef85d7`.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 169 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 14.2 minutes.
- The quick gate includes `mcp`: 43 passed. All seven background pins pass on this head.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. 64 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled; 28.2 minutes. The plan reaches 63 heavy steps plus the release build.
- The heavy failure is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. At `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:79`, the imported mesh has 5,232 facets; the Linux pin expects 6,228. It fails before generation. This round changes no fixture or importer. The failure is outside the four requested MCP findings and is left unchanged.
- The failing test and its STEP fixture have identical Git blobs at the reviewed head, this head, and current `upstream/main`:
  - `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`: `337b27c493810c9ba3f9e68f46ce6c851e1eb6c7`.
  - `testdata/models/Milling-test.step`: `bb4110f4946759a875a71d8387b1c13761c9b28a`.
- The existing known-fail checks for #1950, #2849 and #3825 failed as expected and passed their gate checks.
- The final working tree is clean. HEAD and the base ref did not change during these final-head checks.

The first quick attempt had a generated-cache fault after automatic target seeding: E0463 on internal crates. Cleaning those package artifacts and disabling seeding repaired it. No source change was required.

Goldens moved: none. `example_catalog` passed (39 passed, 4 ignored), and `first_part_programs` passed (2 passed). No recorded program changed.

No UI file changed. Screenshots are not required. No screenshot, log, or review evidence file is in the branch.

## Review fix round on 07e37adeb7a82b1bda741f8003251300db15a291

This round fixes the retained-entity crash from the latest review of `c83ab4889`.
The background lane keeps operation names only. It resolves each entity when it uses the operation.
It skips a queued operation after deletion or undo of its creation.
After History execution, it resolves the current name again before it reads the operation view.
A missing current operation gives a refusal. The `still_current` guard remains before History execution.

### Pin proof

- `background_generate::a_deleted_queued_operation_is_skipped`
- `background_generate::an_undone_queued_add_is_skipped`

Each pin failed with SIGABRT when the reviewed source replaced the fix.
Restoring the fix passed all nine background tests.

### Final-head validation

Head: `07e37adeb7a82b1bda741f8003251300db15a291`.
Base: current `upstream/main`. `16115cd06a3694dfadaa57876c050e6d83c8faab`

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 169 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 15.6 minutes.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12 cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'`: GREEN. 5 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 5.3 minutes. All 11 tests passed.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. 64 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled; 17.9 minutes.
  One observed failure is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.
  At `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:157`, the macOS pin expects `(3158, 3130, 1141)` and receives `(4688, 4660, 1980)`.
  The Linux-only mesh assertion is skipped on this host. This round leaves the test and fixture unchanged.
  Their blobs match current `upstream/main`: test `337b27c493810c9ba3f9e68f46ce6c851e1eb6c7`; fixture `bb4110f4946759a875a71d8387b1c13761c9b28a`.
  No separate baseline run was performed.
- The quick gate ran `example_catalog`: 39 passed, 4 ignored. It also ran `first_part_programs`: 2 passed, and the `adaptive_trochoid` golden suite: 12 passed.

title: fix(2d): a start-side edit of a seeded 2D Offset takes the Arc entry
body:
## What changed

- `EditOperationParams` applies a new law, `OpParams::with_start_side_entry` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/start_side_entry.rs`).
- The law acts on a 2D Offset only. It acts when one edit moves "Pass starts at" from Auto to Inside or Outside, and the entry is Helix before and after the edit. Then the same edit sets Arc.
- The GUI page, MCP `edit_operation`, and the cutting-data and stock edits use the same constructor. Thus each door gets the law.
- One undo restores Auto and Helix together.
- The user's own choice stays:
  - an entry that the same edit changes;
  - a Plunge or Ramp set before the start side moves;
  - a Helix kept on Inside that moves to Outside;
  - a Helix that the user selects again on an Inside or Outside pass;
  - the entry when the start side goes back to Auto.
- The seed (Auto, Helix) does not change. `docs/decisions/3843-start-side-arc.md` records why.

## Cause

`seed_offset2d` seeds Helix for every new 2D Offset. A change of the start side did not change the entry. After #3748, a start-side pass with Helix gives the `EntryNotRecommended` warning. The maintainer said on #3741: "an outside cut would default to a ARC or straight approach in the plane of its cut".

## Tests

Pinning tests:
- `offset_pass_start::start_side_entry::a_start_side_edit_of_a_seeded_offset_takes_arc_and_undo_restores_helix` (command and undo, Inside and Outside).
- `offset_pass_start::start_side_entry::mcp_start_side_edit_takes_arc_and_a_later_helix_choice_stays` (MCP door).
- lib `operation::types::start_side_entry::tests::a_seeded_offset_moved_to_a_start_side_takes_arc`.
- lib `operation::types::start_side_entry::tests::a_user_choice_of_entry_stays`.

Red before the fix: the two integration pins failed on the code without the call in `edit.rs`. The failure text: `assertion left == right failed: Inside enters in the plane of its cut; left: (Inside, Helix); right: (Inside, Arc)`. The MCP pin failed at the `"entry":"arc"` assertion.

Mutations (each red, then restored and green):
- Remove the `before == Helix` guard: `a_user_choice_of_entry_stays` fails.
- Remove the "from Auto" guard: `a_user_choice_of_entry_stays` fails.

Commands on the final head `215d44a52`, base upstream/main `415440375`:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 34 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --only "app suites: example_catalog"`: ok. `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`: ok.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate test pass_start --crate camcraft-ui`: ui lib ok.
- The ignored `offset_pass_start` heavy tests (release step): ok.

Heavy lanes: not run in full. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 64 app steps. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a P3 PR no heavy step, so the light lane ran in its place.

## Goldens moved

None. The example catalog suites ran and pass. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed. The law acts only in an edit, and no golden makes a 2D Offset through a start-side edit.

## Not exercised

- The GUI Lead in page by hand. The page calls the same `EditOperationParams`, and the ui `pass_start` tests pass. No screenshot: the page layout does not change.
- The `EntryNotRecommended` warning itself. It comes from #3748, which is not on main yet. When #3748 merges, the seed Helix on a start side no longer reaches the warning through an edit.
- Pocket and 2D Adaptive. The issue names 2D Offset only.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs` or `crates/app/src/operation/types/`. #3748 (claimed, no PR yet) changes the warning and the Lead in page, not the edit command.

New test file: `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start/start_side_entry.rs` is a submodule of the existing `offset_pass_start` suite. It adds no test binary.

Effort: high
