title: fix(3d): a pass restart in a 3D Pocket level takes the entry type
body:
## What changed

A 3D Pocket pass that restarts after a hop now proves the full cutter disc clear before it keeps a straight restart. The restart axis must lie on an earlier straight cut by the same tool. The whole earlier cut must be at or below the restart depth. Exact endpoints and points on the segment count. There is no XY slack. Arc chords do not count as proof.

Without that proof, a centre-cutting tool takes the operation's entry type first. It then tries a ramp along the pass. If neither fits, it keeps the named plunge fallback. An operation with a Plunge entry keeps that choice. The separate non-centre-cutting core law stays unchanged.

Each candidate runs on a copy. The copy is kept only if it crosses no earlier move and adds no plunge without full-disc clearance. Rejected candidates do not remain in the path.

The policy is in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/reentry.rs`. `ladder.rs` calls it at a pass hop. The decision is in `docs/decisions/3670-pass-hop-entry.md`.

## Cause and review fix

The original pass hop always plunged at the pass start for a centre-cutting tool. The first fix used `plunge_law::into_solid`. That law checks the central core. It does not prove the outer part of the cutter clear.

The latest review found a remaining restart at `(-0.138840, -20.062037, 10)` in the rough-finish catalog case. The stock point `(-0.138840, -17.8, 10)` lies inside the radius-3-mm cutter. The independent OBJ calculation puts the surface at Z8.582312 there. Earlier cuts do not remove that point before the restart.

The full-disc proof is deliberately conservative. Clearance made by several nearby cuts can be missed. The result takes an entry move in that case.

## Pins and mutation proof

- `machining3d::reentry::tests::cleared_core_does_not_prove_the_outer_disc_clear`: a prior cut clears the core but leaves outer stock. A restart on the prior centre line remains clear.
- `machining3d::reentry::tests::an_arc_chord_does_not_prove_a_cleared_disc`: an arc chord does not grant full-disc clearance.
- `catalog_3d_rough_finish::pocket_re_entry_keeps_the_outer_stock_clear` in `camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: reads the OBJ and computes the surface with independent barycentric interpolation. It tracks earlier cutting sweeps at the reviewed stock point. It calls neither clearance predicate.

Existing pins remain:

- `zigzag_helix_re_entries_never_plunge_into_uncut_stock` in `camcraft-motion --test pocket3d_pass_start`.
- `catalog_3d_rough_finish::pocket_re_entries_never_plunge_into_uncut_stock` in `camcraft-app --test example_catalog`.

Mutation proof:

- Restore the core-only policy inside `disc_into_solid`: the new core-versus-disc unit pin fails. The independent catalog pin also fails at move 1390. That move plunges from Z47 to Z10 at `(-0.13884, -20.062037)`, before earlier cuts remove the outer stock point. Restore the fix: both unit pins and the independent catalog pin pass.
- Bypass the first candidate guard: `pocket_re_entries_never_plunge_into_uncut_stock` fails at `(-22.259998, -3.48, 8)`. Restore the guard: both catalog pins pass.

The earlier round also proved both existing pins fail with the old ladder. It proved both fail when the first candidate guard is bypassed. The crossing guard is pinned by `offset_shells::the_shell_entrants_land_on_the_shell`.

## Final-head checks

Head: ea39d4180e62646a463a9b4fa91e3f5464d95254. Base: f2aa981b51a3453428fb294c6c71c575a0178ef6.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 57 steps passed. Tests: 1,155 passed, 44 existing tests ignored, zero failed or stalled.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. The gate ran 103 steps in 30.9 minutes. One step failed unexpectedly. No step stalled.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All six steps passed. All 11 tests passed, with zero failures or stalls.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN. No warnings.
- `app suites: example_catalog`, in the quick gate: 41 passed, four existing tests ignored.
- Reached golden suites: `example_catalog_adaptive`: one passed. `example_catalog_edge_work`: one passed. Both ran in the quick gate.

The quick and heavy gates use `env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`. Clippy also uses `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and `-j6`. The first quick build stopped before tests with stale dependency metadata (`E0463`). Local artifacts for geometry, sim, tools, cl, and kernel were cleaned. The final quick gate passed after that repair. No source changed during the repair.

The heavy gate also records five expected failures. It normalizes them as known failures: #1950 in steps 3, 4, and 77; #3825 in step 72; and #2849 in step 85.

The unexpected failure is `camcraft-app --test pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. The final count check expects `(3158, 3130, 1141)` on macOS arm64. It gets `(4688, 4660, 1980)`. All preceding safety checks pass: no verification warnings, all intended levels cut, no strategy fallback, and no planning-budget refusal.

The same test with the original reviewed `reentry.rs` gets the same counts and fails at the same check. This count-pin drift predates this review fix. The test is left unchanged because this round fixes only the latest review finding. The final source is restored, and the worktree is clean. The heavy gate remains RED.

## Goldens moved

Regeneration command: `cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rough-finish`.

- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc`: replaces the remaining straight restarts without full-disc clearance with entry moves.
- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.camproj`: updates the saved pocket toolpath cache to match the regenerated program.

Regeneration passed. Only these two catalog files changed. The pocket section now has zero straight plunges at F300, down from ten. Both downstream NC finish sections remain byte-identical. Their saved move arrays also remain unchanged. Regeneration updates only the operation stamps in those two saved finish entities.

## Not exercised

No machine run. No screenshots, because this change has no UI effect. The heavy gate does not pass because of the pre-existing count mismatch described above.

The two additional items from #3670 remain in #3852: feeds from the hop plane over cleared stock, and moves shorter than the post resolution.

Changelog: 3D Pocket: a pass that starts again inside a level now enters by the operation's helix or ramp (or a ramp along the pass) instead of a straight plunge into uncut stock.

Fixes #3670

title: fix(2d): read the fig8 part wall as one wall, and try the edge route before a pass-link lift
body:
## What changed

The fig8 lifts of #3824 and #3825 have one cause, and it is not in `pass_link`.

- **Cause.** `level_rings::sides` splits the boundary of the cutter-centre area into ring 0 (the start side) and the walls. It used a side tolerance (`SIDE_EPS`) of 1 um. The area and the start side are two offsets, and each flattens the same round joins within 5 um (`ARC_TOL_UNITS`). On fig8, at X about +-46.5 and Y about 123.2, the band is 5 mm wide. There, two 0.117 mm stretches of the part wall read as the stock side.
  - Inside: the wall ring had a gap at each stretch, and each gap gave a lift.
  - Outside: the two stretches were ring 0 and were cut first. Each was reached by a lift across the part and entered by a plunge into material (the four links of #3825).
- **Fix 1** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs`): `SIDE_EPS` is now 10 um, twice the flattening error.
- **Fix 2** (`ring_links.rs`, `ladder_links.rs`): as #3824 asks, the pass link round a part tries `edge_route` after the straight chord. Each chord of the route gets the proof of the straight chord (`chord_proof`: certified area, no crossing of `passes` and `st.level`, each sample in air or over a cut column). The whole route is within the stay-down limit. `pass_link` records the route as a cut of the level. A lift stays only when the chord and the route both fail, and it keeps the straight chord's reason. On the cases below, this change alone changes no reading. It closes the gap that the review of #3818 found.

## Readings (release)

| Reading | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| fig8 Inside, lifts inside a level | 6 | 0 |
| fig8 Outside, lifts inside a level | 12 | 3 (one short hop each level, named "would cut uncut stock with the full tool width") |
| fig8 Outside, lifts across the part | 4 each level | 0 |
| fig8 Outside, "plunged into material" notes (Helix and Arc entry) | 6 | 0 |
| `flute_reach`, 10 mm flute, rapid findings | 9 | 3 |
| clamp case (`pass_start_levels::ring_links::lift_reason_is_named`), Inside / Outside lifts | 3 / 26 | 4 / 26, each named |

The clamp case: its Inside pass start (-3.29, 15.66) is where the clamp's rounded keep-out meets the part ring almost at a tangent. The meeting point moves by micrometres with the side tolerance (2 lifts at 2 um, 4 lifts from 3 um to 10 um). The decision file records this.

"Before" for fig8 is the run with only Fix 2 in place: Inside 6, Outside 12, the same 18 lifts (9 crossing, 9 area) that #3824 reports, and the six plunge notes of #3825.

## Pinning tests

- `offset_pass_start::lifts::fig8_start_sides_lift_only_with_a_named_reason`: now also asserts at most 0 lifts on Inside and 3 on Outside.
- `offset_pass_start::lifts::fig8_outside_pass_links_keep_off_the_part_and_enter_on_cut_floor` (new, heavy lane): no pass link lifts over the part, and no "plunged into material" note.
- `offset_pass_start::fig8_outside_offset_has_no_plunge_into_material` (from #3823): the `known-fail #3825` marker and the `// known-fail-assert` line are removed. It is now a plain heavy-lane pin, and it passes.
- `flute_reach::a_ten_mm_flute_names_its_cause_before_the_rapid_findings`: now asserts at most 3 rapid findings.
- Crossing and overcut: `fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing`, `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (21 points or fewer), and the `pass_start_levels::ring_links` shape masks (`assert_no_overcut`, `assert_no_crossing`) stay green.

## Gates

All on the final head (`f5e3155dc`, origin/main with #3823, #3837 and #3822 merged in):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 173 steps (motion lib, the motion and app suites of the gate map), each green.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --only`: `app heavy: offset_pass_start`, `app heavy: flute_reach`, `app heavy: pocket_pass_start` and `motion heavy: pass_start_levels`: each ok. On the head before #3837: `app heavy: known fail #2849 ...` stays red as expected.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start --test flute_reach -- -D warnings`: clean.
- New unit pin: `machining2d::ring_side::tests::the_side_tolerance_keeps_a_real_short_wall_and_drops_a_flat_sliver` (a 0.1 mm wall stretch 50 um off the start side stays a wall; a stretch 5 um off reads as the start side).

## Not exercised

- No test reaches the new edge-route branch of `ring_links::link` with a route that passes the proof. On fig8 and the box fixtures, the two ends of each failed link stand on different loops of the area, or the pass start stands in uncut stock. Each chord of a route uses the proven `chord_proof`, so the route cannot post a chord that the straight link would refuse.
- No app window was opened. The private models in `testdata/models` were not used.

title: fix(sim): refuse a feed plunge deeper than one stepdown below the uncut floor
body:
## What changed

The verifier names a feed plunge that takes more than one stepdown of uncut material in one move (#3679, law (d3)).

- New law `camcraft_sim::verify::plunge_depth`: every non-rapid axial descent is judged against the floor that the cuts before it left under the full tool disc. The take is the move's own bite - the lesser of the move's start and that floor - so a tip that a rapid already stood inside stock answers for its own descent only. A dive from air keeps the full column reading.
- The gate is `VerifyContext::plunge_stepdown`, the `None` discipline: only the level-cutting kinds state a stepdown (2D Contour, Pocket, Offset2D, Slot, TrochoidalSlot, Adaptive2D, Pocket3D, MultiAxisRough, the staged Face). A tilted 3+2 frame keeps `None`.
- The finding is advisory by the #3525 pattern: `Warning::PlungeTooDeep { at, mm, limit_mm }`, MCP kind `plunge_too_deep`, UI line 227. The post is not held. The issue's crescent case (an 18 mm plunge beside stock that no level above cut) is named.
- The program ahead acquits a conviction: `acquit_plunge_by_prior` re-reads each finding against the prior program's surface, the same third term of the min that `acquit_by_prior` gives a rapid. The wiring in `generate.rs` cuts the prior grid when either law convicted.
- The slack stays the established `z_tol` alone. No wider slack was added: the 0.5 mm overage of the first commit was a floor error and a bite error, not a tolerance error.

## The six reconciled suites

The first commit (cc1bed29d) over-convicted six pre-existing app tests. All six keep their expected verdicts. No test was changed.

1. `vertical_rapid_stock.rs::a_vertical_rapid_into_a_taller_block_is_named_and_blocks_the_post` - the entry rapid broke the raw top and the feed below it took 2 mm. The bite reading acquits the feed; the rapid conviction stands and holds the post.
2. `vertical_rapid_stock.rs::a_dive_into_stock_an_earlier_face_removed_posts` - the face left Z 5 standing. The bite reading and the prior acquittal clear the dive.
3. `carried_stock_entry.rs` (both `assert_safe_entry` failures) - 18 trochoidal microlift plunges of 0.3 mm read the raw 10.5 column; the bite reading acquits them. The one contour plunge read 10.5 where the face had left 10.0, its stepdown exactly; the prior acquittal clears it.
4. `clearance_in_stock.rs::the_same_plane_over_stock_an_earlier_face_cut_down_holds_only_for_the_first_traverse` - the prior acquittal removes the advisory; the first traverse stands as before.
5. `top_stock.rs::facing_to_top_removes_the_height_warning_but_a_shallow_face_does_not` - the same face-acquitted dive; the warnings are empty again.
6. The slack question - the 0.5 mm overage was cured by the honest floor and the honest bite, not by a wider tolerance. The law keeps the established `z_tol`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-sim` `plunge_depth` binary: the crescent dive is named (mm 18.0 against the 4.5 stepdown); a dive exactly one stepdown deep, a ring-entry dive in the kerf of the level above, a pecked dive and the `None` gate stay clean; the bite is pinned by `a_feed_that_a_rapid_already_stood_inside_stock_answers_for_its_own_bite_only` and `a_feed_plunge_buried_deeper_than_one_stepdown_is_named_for_its_own_bite`.
- `camcraft-sim` `verify::prior` units: the plunge acquittal over a cleared pocket, the dive below the prior floor that still stands, the wider tool, the lateral feed, the limit no number can read.
- `camcraft-app` `plunge_depth_tab`: the catalog case `2d/contour-tabs` names its three tab-window dives (6.0 mm against a 2.0 stepdown), advisory.
- The six reconciled suites above.

## What was not exercised

- The solids-based re-read of a stepped stock (`acquit_by_stock_top`) is not wired for the feed plunge: a plunge into a casting's low step still reads the raw grid's top. Named under Limits in `docs/decisions/3679-plunge-depth-law.md`.
- The heavy lanes and the pixel snapshots did not run; the quick gate ran only. The example catalog suites other than the pinned tab case did not run.
- The tilted 3+2 frames stay unnamed until a pose-aware reading exists.

## Follow-up

- #3722 stays open: decide whether a named over-deep dive stands as a proven floor for the later laws (`Rest::cut` clears its own column).

Changelog: verify names a feed plunge that takes more than one stepdown of uncut material in one move, judged on the move's own bite and acquitted on prior-cut material (advisory `plunge_too_deep`, the post is not held) (#3679)

Fixes #3679

AI Chat classifies cloud provider authentication failures and displays a safe key rejected status.

title: perf(sim): grow the column stock's cut history in place
body:
### What changed

- `stock_sim::cut::simulate` no longer copies the column stock's whole cut history at the start of each call. It takes the history out, grows it with `Arc::make_mut`, and puts it back. `Arc::make_mut` copies the history only when another stock shares it.
- On a refusal, the code truncates the cuts to their old count and puts the history back. `add_ops` only appends cuts, so the stock stays as it was.
- The behaviour of a single call does not change. A program that is cut one move for each call is now linear in its moves, not quadratic.

### Readings

- New pin `a_call_grows_the_history_in_place` on the v0.26.0 code: FAILED (`simulate copied the history instead of growing it in place`). With this change: ok.
- 4000 one-move calls on a 200 x 200 column block (debug build, this machine): 1.649 s before, 0.514 s after. The stock is the same to the bit as the one-call cut, before and after.
- A 3-axis job of 137,940 moves on a 2541 x 2100 column stock, cut one move for each call: more than 1800 s before (stopped), 6 s after. The removed volume is the same to the bit as the one-call cut.

### Pinning tests

- `stock_sim::cut::history_tests::a_call_grows_the_history_in_place`: the history keeps its allocation across two calls, and the cuts are added.
- `stock_sim::cut::history_tests::a_shared_history_is_copied_before_it_grows`: a clone keeps its own history and its columns when the other stock is cut.
- `stock_columns::one_move_for_each_call_is_the_one_call_cut`: 4000 one-move calls give the one-call stock to the bit. This test joins the existing `stock_columns` binary. It adds no new test binary.

### Gates

- Quick gate on the final head (ffe6b6e86, after a merge of upstream main): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 83 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (20.8 min).
- Pinning tests on the final head: `history_tests` 2/2, `stock_columns` 4/4.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the final head: clean.
- Light gate (`cargo xtask gate light`) on the first head e8f8d3b2c: 4 steps, 0 failed. The merge of main added no code of this PR.
- The new pin on the v0.26.0 `cut.rs`: FAILED, as expected. On this branch: ok.

### Not exercised

- The field engine and the carried stock. `carried::clip_columns_under` has the same copy, but it runs one time for each setup, not for each move. This PR does not change it.
- The heavy lanes (they run at the cut).
- The refusal path is not reached by a test: `check_ops` and the posed-move check refuse before the history changes, and I found no input that makes `add_ops` or `read` refuse after the history is taken out.

Fork synced at v0.26.0. The branch was refreshed with a merge of upstream main (contributor mode: merge, no rebase). The two conflicts were in process files only (`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`); main's version was taken. The diff against main is now the three files of this fix.

title: fix(motion): ring links only for ring sets, lift to the user's pass plane
body:
## What changed

- **Ring law only for ring sets.** A new predicate `ring_links::rings` (`Waterline | OffsetRings`, the strategy of the posted passes) gates `ring_links::for_side` at both callers: `pocket.rs` and the plain source of `pocket_avoid.rs`.
  - Zigzag rows round a part keep the links that they had before #3818.
  - The 2D Pocket with Outside containment stays under the ring law (the coordinator's decision). It now has pins.
  - 2D Adaptive is no ring set. Where the HSM plan runs its own spiral round a part (Outside with a stock outline, the air plan of #3355), the ring law does not link it, and it posts the moves of main before #3818 (pinned).
  - Where the HSM plan cannot start on the start side (a hole wall Inside; on the dog bone also Outside), it falls back to Offset rings, and a note names the fallback. Those passes are rings. The planner joins them by the in-air law of #3747 (`level_order`), so the pass links also use the ring law. They are pinned as for the pocket.
- **A failed ring link honours `Link::Clearance`.** In `ladder_links::pass_link`, a failed ring link lifts to `clearance_z` when the user chose Clearance for the pass link. With Retract, KeepDown or the default, it lifts to `hop_z` as before. The link tally (`links.rs`) now records the plane, and the `link:` note says "lifted to the clearance height" for that case. The default text does not change.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3822-pocket-ring-scope.md`.

## The Adaptive pins

The brief asked for "Adaptive Spiral output equals main before #3818". That pin is `adaptive_spiral_round_a_part_outside_equals_main_before_3818`: the square fixture of `pocket_hsm_start_tests` with `around_part: true` and Outside, where the spiral runs (no fallback). Its digest equals the digest read on `b2ff0ef1b`, the first parent of the #3818 merge. With the predicate removed the pin is red (checked). On the dog bone, Adaptive always falls back to Offset rings, and those rings are pinned by the ring law. The Zigzag pin also equals main before #3818, and it is red without the predicate (checked).

## Overlap

The #3824 worker also edits `ladder_links::pass_link`. This PR adds the `(Some(Err(why)), Link::Clearance)` arm there, which lifts to `clearance_z` and calls `tally.lift_to(.., CLEARANCE_PLANE, ..)`. The PR that merges second must keep that arm.

## Pinning tests (`camcraft-motion`, `pass_start_levels::pocket_outside`)

- `outside_pocket_rings_round_a_disc_do_not_lift`: Waterline and Offset rings, Inside and Outside. 0 lifts and 0 re-entries, no overcut (shape mask), no crossing feeds, each lift named.
- `outside_pocket_dog_bone_names_each_lift`: the same laws on the #3744 dog bone.
- `failed_ring_link_lifts_to_the_users_pass_plane`: a clamp across the link, on both ring strategies. Clearance lifts to 10.0 (clearance), and Retract and KeepDown lift to 2.0 (retract). Each lift is named, and the note names the plane.
- `zigzag_rows_keep_their_links_round_a_part`: the digest equals main before #3818.
- `adaptive_spiral_round_a_part_outside_equals_main_before_3818`: the Adaptive air-plan spiral round a part, Outside, equals main before #3818.
- `adaptive_fallback_rings_link_by_the_ring_law`: the fallback is named, no overcut, no crossing, each lift named.

- Rework head (after `git merge origin/main`, which includes #3823): `pass_start_levels` 19 passed; `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test pocket_pass_start` 5 passed, 2 ignored; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

title: fix(2d): start-side Arc entry plunges in air outside the stock box
body:
## What changed

A 2D Offset pass that starts Inside or Outside round a part now enters by the Arc entry from the air outside the stock box (new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/air_entry.rs`).

1. The tool plunges in air at a point P. The distance from P to the stock box is at least the tool radius plus `approach_distance` (#3745).
2. In the cut plane, a straight lead in air (tangent to the arc), then one G17 arc of Arc radius and Arc sweep, tangent to the first cut at the pass start. A change of Arc radius or Arc sweep changes the arc in the output.
3. The lead is proved with the proof of the horizontal arc entry (`descent_xy::arc_at`, made `pub(super)`) against the cutter-centre area joined with the air outside the box, and across none of the planned passes. Thus it touches no part and crosses no ring.
4. When no air lead fits, the entry stands down to a named helix, then a named ramp along the first cut, else the op is refused by name (`AIR_ENTRY_REFUSAL`, read by `approach::refusal`). The axial dive and the vertical arc ramp into material are no longer stand-ins.
5. A re-entry after a lift onto a start in material (`entry_restart`) tries the air entry first. On a start-side pass it then tries a clear helix before the named plunge.
6. The avoid route (fixtures and clamps, #3810): each level takes the same air room, less that level's keep-outs over the whole descent. A plunge or lead that would touch a fixture or a clamp is not proved, so the entry moves or stands down by name.

Inside: the other rings enclose the first Inside ring, so each lead from the air crosses rings at the cut Z. The verifier's Crossing law holds such a post. Thus Inside takes the named helix (or ramp), never a plunge into material. The decision and the dropped options are in `docs/decisions/3746-air-entry.md`.

The pass links (`level_link`, `pass_link`, `link_proof`) are not changed (#3747 owns them).

## Readings (dog bone, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, Arc entry)

- Before: Outside plunged at (39.400, -24.400), 0.000 mm off the stock box, note "the arc's lead room is blocked - axial dive on the floor instead". Inside entered with the vertical arc, whose first chords are a plunge into material by `plunge_law::first_solid_plunge`.
- After: Outside plunges 6 mm or more off the box (R 4 + approach 2); the first cut is a G17 arc of radius 8 (Arc radius 0) and a quarter turn (Arc sweep 0); radius 6 / 10 and sweep 60 show in the output. Inside: no plunge into material; the entry is named.
- fig8 Outside, Arc entry: each level is entered from the air with a first arc. After the merge of #3818, four pass links still lift across the part to a start inside ring 0, and those re-entries plunge into material, named. An air lead would cross ring 0 at the cut Z; no helix or ramp fits clear of the cut rings. The cause is the link code: #3825.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `machining2d::air_entry::tests`: `outside_entry_plunges_in_air`, `outside_first_cut_is_an_arc_in_the_plane`, `arc_radius_changes_the_lead`, `inside_entry_is_no_plunge_into_material`, `outside_entry_is_no_plunge_into_material`. All five were red with the air room off (the `main` behaviour) and are green now.
- `camcraft-app` `offset_pass_start` (heavy): `fig8_start_sides_enter_from_the_air` (green).
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `avoid_route_entry_plunges_in_air_clear_of_a_clamp` (#3810; red with the avoid air room off).
- `fig8_outside_offset_has_no_plunge_into_material`: known-fail #3825 (still red after #3818: the four re-entry plunges come from pass-link lifts).

## Gates

On the head after the merge of origin/main (with #3818):
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6): 172 steps, 0 failed.
- Targeted heavy step `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: offset_pass_start"`: ok; the gate skipped the known-fail pin of #3825.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- A user-selected Helix, Ramp or Plunge keeps its entry; its warning and the Arc default are #3748.
- The Lead in / Lead out page already offers all four kinds for each start side and greys none out (`lead_page.rs`). No UI change.
- The light lane was not run.
- `descent.rs` was 411 lines and is 418 now (the new `Descent::Air` arms).

Changelog: 2D Offset "Pass starts at" Inside and Outside: the Arc entry plunges in air outside the stock box (tool radius plus the approach distance) and arcs onto the first ring in the cut plane with the Arc radius and Arc sweep; where no air entry fits, a named helix or ramp is used, never a plunge into material.

Effort: max

Fixes #3746
Fixes #3810

Use the specified bull-nose corner radius to check straight, upright cuts for a gouge in the native Envelope verifier. The check reports remaining stock as unmeasured.

- The explicit and implicit ball profiles produce identical warnings on the same rail. The existing numeric ball-envelope test also passes.

- Windows native quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) passed all six steps on `f48a9aaf6`. It ran 270 tests with zero failures or skips.

title: fix(2d): name narrow stock bands in generation refusals
body:
## What changed

Name the stock band around the part when a stock-source pocket-family operation refuses because the cutter cannot fit.
The reported reproduction now names the 2.000 mm minimum side width and the 3.000 mm tool.
The refusal also names stock to leave per wall and suggests a smaller tool, wider stock, or a 2D Contour.
True pockets keep their existing refusal, with a part selection and with the stock as the source.
Curved bands receive advice without an invented width.
Generation still refuses the same job and emits no path.

The band message applies only when the area surrounds kept material.
A piece of the stock-minus-part region is a band when its outer loop is a loop of the stock outline, and material stands inside that loop.
A closed pocket and a pocket around an island have part walls as their boundary. They keep the pocket refusal.
A strip of stock beside a part that is flush with the other stock sides also keeps the pocket refusal.

## Cause

The generator reports a generic pocket error before the successful-path band note can run.
The app holds the stock-source context needed to explain that error.

## Tests

Final head: `0d316a6dc57c22d007e08e89c13828e1b5643156`.
Gate base: current `upstream/main` at `cd0222d9cceb5e6f831a13071b93f1d083c3f10e`.

title: fix(ai): use installed local models and current cloud defaults
body:
## What changed

An empty local model field selects an installed Ollama model that can call tools.
The transport reads `/api/tags` and checks each candidate with `/api/show`.
All three local presets use this selection rule and keep their fallback modes.
An explicit model name remains the user's choice.
Malformed model lists stop with a named diagnostic.
If no model qualifies, the message gives `ollama pull ornith-1.5:35b` and the model library URL.
For a local provider, the panel shows an automatic-selection hint and a clickable library link.
An empty cloud Model field displays and uses the shared provider default.
Cloud requests do not select an installed local model.

The automatic selection has a time limit: 5 s for each request and 20 s for the whole selection.
The model list request and each model probe use the remaining total time as an additional limit.
A failed probe of one model does not stop the selection. The next model is checked.
Each cause has its own message:

- The server did not answer its model list. The message gives `ollama serve`.
- No installed model can call tools. The message gives the install command.
- The probe failed for a named model, and no other model can call tools.
- The time limit ended. The message gives the count of checked models.

A chat failure after an automatic selection names the selected model.

One shared table holds the cloud defaults:

- Anthropic: `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
- OpenAI Chat and Responses: `gpt-6.2-sol`.
- Gemini: `gemini-4-hydrogen`.

The catalog test rejects a default when its table row marks it retired.
The table needs maintenance when providers change model availability.

<details>
<summary>UI before and after</summary>

Before:

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b00d2ce26fb791475d28089e4cae74cb9fe13451/issue-3782-model-defaults/before.png)

After:

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b00d2ce26fb791475d28089e4cae74cb9fe13451/issue-3782-model-defaults/after.png)

</details>

## Cause

The presets used fixed model IDs.
The local transport did not list installed models.
Native mode probed the fixed name and could fail before the first chat request.

Readings: [Ollama model list](https://docs.ollama.com/api/tags), [Anthropic models](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview), [OpenAI model](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.2-sol), [Gemini model](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-hydrogen).

## Tests

Final head: `94478ac2b6c353808d8a277120713265dfb52367`.
Tested upstream main: `fd7ad703d5233938d1892313c1e69fa4710c99e6`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. 14 steps: 13 passed, 1 failed, 0 stalled. 1,900 tests passed; 7 failed; 8 ignored. The UI library step failed because wgpu found no graphics adapter on this host. The timeout pins passed in this run..
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on the final head..
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: passed on the final head: 39 passed; 4 ignored..

Pin proof for this round (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/transport_discovery_tests.rs`):

- `ollama_discovery_caps_the_model_list_by_the_total_time`
- `ollama_discovery_caps_a_probe_by_the_remaining_total_time`

Both slow-response pins failed with the source fix reverted. Both passed after the fix was restored.
The probe pin also failed with a static total timeout instead of the remaining total time.
That mutation took 1.5168 s and exceeded the test's 1.3 s bound.
After restoration, all six discovery tests passed.

Earlier fix rounds recorded red/green mutation proof for failed-probe continuation, separate failure diagnostics, the selection time limit, and the selected model name.
They also recorded red/green proof for the empty cloud Model default and the install guidance.
The latest review confirmed that those focused tests passed on `4fbbf7bde`.
Those earlier results are not final-head gate results.

Heavy lanes: not applicable.
The PR changes AI transport and panel code. This round changes the discovery timeout and its tests.
The diff changes no app operation, motion, simulation, post, or geometry code.

## Goldens moved

None. The example catalog suite ran on the final head. No recorded NC, CL, or catalog file differs in `git diff upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "examples/catalog/**"`. The worktree is clean..

![Cloud Model before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/f8c2b8201ee795fffa0b7f4ae1b1f5fa1657d605/pr-3799/review-fix-2026-11-24/cloud-before.png)

The headless harness rendered these images in an earlier round.

title: fix(ui): add AI Chat key setup and provider readiness
body:
## What changed

AI Chat can save, replace, remove, and test a provider API key.
It uses the existing OS keychain entries and environment-first lookup.
The entry field clears after save, cancel, and provider changes.
The panel never draws a stored key.

The panel checks cloud readiness when the provider or offline setting changes.
Editing a cloud Model does not read the keychain again.
Ollama Model edits wait for a 500 ms pause before one readiness check.
A cloud Model edit after a finished Test replaces the Test result with "Model changed. Click Test to test this model."
The settings code reads `camcraft_app::clock::Instant`, because the std clock panics in the browser build.
The status names a missing key, an unavailable Ollama server, or a missing model.
Ready means that a key was found. It does not prove that the provider accepted it.
Test sends a small request to the selected model. The provider can bill this request.
Credential and network work runs in the background.

The setup help and guide explain keys, billing, OS permission prompts, and Ollama setup.
They include `ollama serve`, server check commands, `OLLAMA_HOST`, `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`, and `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE`.
They state that a Gemini app subscription does not include an API key.
The help states the current endpoint limit.
Remove deletes the stored key only. It does not revoke a key or remove an environment variable.

Effort: medium

## Remaining work

This PR supplies part of #3781. It does not close that issue.

- #3803 tracks the ignored `live-ai` smoke tests for all providers, including key lookup, Ready, text, and `get_job`.
- #3804 tracks a distinct key-rejected status for a wrong key.

The reporter's macOS hand-test waits until the live lane in #3803 runs.
Keep this PR a draft while that requirement remains open.

After that lane runs, use this checklist:

1. Open View > Panels > AI Chat. Choose a cloud provider. Check its key and billing links.
2. Save a key. Confirm that the entry clears and the status names the key source.
3. If macOS asks, enter the login keychain password in its prompt. Choose Always Allow. Select Test.
4. Send a read-only greeting. Replace the key and test again. Remove it and check the status.
5. Check the other cloud help. Select Ollama and check its server and Model status.

They contain no actual key. The help text added in this review round needs a refreshed screenshot: capture was attempted, but the GPU renderer returned `No adapter found` (`CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError`). This host cannot render the updated help views.

title: ci(release): package the Arch build from the Linux release binaries
body:
## What changed

- `.github/workflows/aur-package.yml` compiles nothing now. It downloads the `linux-packages` artifact of the same run. It unpacks `camcraft-ui`, `camcraft-cli` and `post` from `camcraft-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`.
- `makepkg -o --noprepare -d` gets, checks and extracts the recipe source. Then `makepkg -R -d` runs only `package()` around the prebuilt binaries.
- A CI copy of the recipe (`PKGBUILD.prebuilt`, not committed) adds `'!strip' '!debug'`. makepkg then does not change the binaries.
- A new check compares the SHA256 of each packaged binary with the binary in the Linux tarball. A difference fails the job. On a tag run, the tarball version must agree with the tag.
- A dispatch run packages the assets of its own checkout, because its binaries come from that checkout.
- The job installs only `base-devel` and `curl`. It installs no Rust and no library headers.
- `aur/PKGBUILD` and `aur/.SRCINFO` do not change. They stay the from-source recipe for AUR users. The `.SRCINFO` check still runs.
- `release.yml`: one comment line on the `aur` job. No trigger and no `on:` block changed.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3773-aur-reuse-linux.md`.

## Readings

- Tag run 45269109413 (v0.25.0): `aur / build` ran 21:42:18 -> 22:31:11, that is 48 min 53 s, about 49 billed Linux minutes.
- `publish` waited for the AUR job for 30 minutes after the last other platform (macOS ended at 22:01:16).
- Expected after: about 2-4 minutes (container pull, `pacman -Syu base-devel curl`, artifact download, `makepkg -R`). Expected saving: about 45 billed minutes for each tag run. The release page goes out about 30 minutes earlier.

## How tested

- Both workflow files parse as YAML (`yaml.safe_load`).
- Each `run:` script of the AUR job passes `bash -n`.
- The `options=` sed edit was run on `aur/PKGBUILD`. It gives `options=('!lto' '!strip' '!debug')`, and the guard `grep` matches.

## Not exercised

- The job did not run. A `workflow_dispatch` of `release.yml` without `site_only` builds all platforms, which is a full release run. `site_only` skips `linux` and thus `aur`. No Docker is on this machine for a local Arch container run.
- The first real run is the next tag run, or a dispatch that the maintainer starts.

This is a `.github` change. It waits for the maintainer's read (`needs-maintainer`).

title: fix(post): keep decimal points in Fanuc-family feed words
body:
## What changed

Keep decimal points in Fanuc, Doosan DNM and Mazak feed words.
Keep them on the separate capped rotary feeds in Fanuc and Doosan DNM.
Keep the existing conversion, precision, rounding and rate limits.

Record the manual audit for all 17 posts in [the decision record](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/9c3d2888e36611daea6f02720cf79d3c440350bf/docs/decisions/3690-feed-decimals.md).
Update exact test expectations and regenerate the affected NC programs.

## Cause

The formatters removed the decimal point from whole feeds.
A request for 2 inch/min became F2.
The cited controls can read that unpointed word as 0.02 inch/min.
An explicit point makes the unit clear.

## Tests

Committed head: 9c3d2888e36611daea6f02720cf79d3c440350bf.
Full verification started from upstream main 7868d378680b325246b0dcdcdbf76c421f801cd9.
The checks cover the committed source and NC programs.
The decision record was added after verification.

Pin command: `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test control_feed_decimal_point -- --nocapture`.
All five pins failed on unchanged production code.
All five passed with the fix.

- `fanuc_whole_inch_feeds_keep_their_decimal_point`
- `doosan_whole_inch_feeds_keep_their_decimal_point`
- `mazak_whole_inch_feeds_keep_their_decimal_point`
- `fanuc_capped_inch_feed_keeps_its_decimal_point`
- `doosan_capped_inch_feed_keeps_its_decimal_point`

Mutation results:

- Restore the full old Fanuc script: ordinary and capped pins fail. Restore the fix: both pass.
- Restore the full old Doosan script: ordinary and capped pins fail. Restore the fix: both pass.
- Restore the full old Mazak script: the ordinary pin fails. Restore the fix: it passes.
- Remove only the Fanuc capped point, with its ordinary formatter fixed: the capped pin fails. Restore: it passes.
- Remove only the Doosan capped point, with its ordinary formatter fixed: the capped pin fails. Restore: it passes.

Seven pin results proved red without the relevant fix and green after the restore.

- The quick run also passed `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`: one test each.

- That retry passed all 4 ignored catalog tests and both expected known-fail checks. The other 61 heavy steps passed unchanged.

- `git diff --check`: passed.

The final coverage has no unresolved failure.
Expected text and golden updates explain the initial red steps.
One cache-enabled prebuild run waited after compilation, as in #3675. Only that gate session was interrupted.
Retries used forced Cargo environment settings for the wrapper and target seed.
Missing local build artifacts required package cleanup in this worktree. No shared cache service stopped.

New test binary: No feed-format directory suite exists.
The cross-post decimal pins use a separate binary with a Gate map for the three changed posts.

97 NC programs changed. Each row below has the same reason: add decimal points to integer F words to make their units explicit.

The only changes add 27,691 F decimal points.

body:
## What changed

- `posting_plasma.rs`: the plasma clause keeps each warning of the laws as data. The new type is `posting::GateWarning { op, kind, message }`. The kinds are `plasma_tip_up` and `plasma_kerf_crossing`. A refusal stays a gate problem.
- `posting.rs`: `GateReport` has a new `warnings` field. `verification_report_by` fills it from the plasma clause.
- `script/api.rs` (`v_verify`): each gate warning goes into the `warnings` row of its operation. It also goes into a new `gate.warnings` list, with the op label. `ok` and `held_by` do not change, because the laws warn and do not refuse.
- `mcp/job.rs` (`verify`): each gate warning is a finding. The finding has the op label, `move: null`, the kind, the message and `blocks_post: false`.
- The `not_judged` line does not change. The G-code viewer header shows only this line, so the UI keeps the warnings.

## Cause

The plasma clause put its warnings into one sentence in `gate.not_judged`. Nothing else carried them. `findings`, the op `warnings` and `ok` read a clean program.

## Tests

- Pin: `mcp_plasma::plasma_mcp_verify_lists_a_tip_up_as_a_finding_and_an_operation_warning`. The test saves a cache with two parts. The rapid into C1 crosses the freed part C0. The test then runs MCP `verify`. It asserts one `plasma_tip_up` finding for `Plasma1` with `blocks_post: false`, the same text in the op `warnings`, no gate problem, an empty `held_by`, and `ok: true`.
- Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code, `findings` was `[]` and the warning was only in `not_judged` (`left: 0, right: 1`).
- Mutations (each run on the pin, then restored):
  - `mcp/job.rs` back to upstream/main: red (no finding).
  - The op-row push in `gate_warnings` removed: red (the op warnings assert).
  - The `GateWarning` push in `plasma_clause` removed: red (no finding).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `cd3669c58`: 307 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `mcp_plasma` and `plasma_gate`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P3` PR. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a heavy step only to a `P1` PR.

## Goldens moved

None. I ran `git diff --stat upstream/main -- '*.nc' '*.cl' 'examples/catalog/**'`: no change. The example catalog suites pass. The change does not touch a generator or a post.

## Not exercised

- The QA project `q06-bracket.camproj` itself. The pin builds the same law result (a rapid over a freed part) on a small fixture.
- A kerf-crossing warning end to end. It uses the same code path as the tip-up; only the kind name is different.
- The UI. No UI code changed. The viewer header still reads `not_judged`.
- A change to the cut order or the rapid route that avoids the freed slugs. That is generator work. It is not in this PR.

title: feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal
body:
feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal

## What changed

Issue #2772, parts 1 and 2 of the plan in
`docs/decisions/2772-rotary-4axis-refusal.md`. The rotary kinds
(Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) read their rotation
axis from a STATEMENT first; today's free fit is the fallback, and
nothing stated keeps every behaviour bit for bit.

1. The stated-axis resolver, `camcraft_app::rotary_stated` over
   `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_stated`:
   - the op's own `stated_axis` direction first, else the mounted
     machine's stated rotary lines (a stated `axis` vector, else the
     RS-274 letter's line - the index-swing clause's own
     `rotary_line` reading, so one law reads both doors);
   - each line anchored through the setup's work offset origin (the
     indexed post's setup law: the WCS sits on the rotary
     centreline), canonicalized the fit's own way (signed, pinned to
     the `o . u = 0` foot), so a part truly on the line keeps the
     fitted path move for move;
   - JUDGED, never trusted: the fit's own concurrency share,
     coarseness skip and bearing law about the stated line
     (`axis_stated::judged_any`). A disagreement refuses by name:
     the part's own fitted axis and the two acts that fix it when
     the model is a revolve placed off the line; the freeform's
     4-axis wording (with the pinned "share no rotation axis"
     words) when no axis fits at all. Never a silent fall back to a
     free fit when a line was stated. A stated line that leans or is
     no direction refuses by name, as the swing clause does.
2. The caller switch, stated first / fit fallback:
   - `fixture::rotary_axis_of` - feeds the sim's chord pass
     (`stock_sim_rotary::rotary_plan`), the first traverse and the
     post gate's struck-steel law (`fixture_struck`): all three
     follow with no change of their own;
   - `first_traverse::turned_axis` - already prefers the job axis,
     which is now the stated-or-fitted line;
   - `rotary_law::rotary_into` - the radial field verdict takes the
     job's resolved axis (`rotary_axis`), keeping its fail-closed
     Gouge for the nothing-known case;
   - `rotary_picks::usable` and the centre-cutting audit's
     `revolved_bar_stated` - judge and read the resolved axis;
   - the letter door `rotary_gate::letter_gate` (moved from
     generate.rs) - a stated line answers the letter without a fit,
     held to the machine inventory;
   - the three motion kernels grow `*_stated` entries
     (`rotary_contour_stated`, `rotary_parallel_over_stated`,
     `rotary_offset_stated`) that take the judged axis; the plain
     entries keep the fit inside, so turning, drilling and every
     existing golden path are untouched.
3. The op param: `stated_axis` on the three arms - a direction
   ratio, never unit-scaled (the machine file's own law for its
   `axis` vector), through the WCS origin, overriding the machine
   line. UI edit (the rotary page's Passes tab, an armed group of
   three direction numbers riding the existing EditOperationParams
   commit), MCP patch (`edit_operation`'s merge patch over the DTO,
   automatic), project round-trip (`stated_axis`, PROJECT_VERSION
   steps v77 -> v78: an older reader must refuse rather than drop
   the statement and turn the part about an axis the user never
   named).
4. The cache stamp: the op's own direction, the machine's stated
   lines and the WCS anchor enter the digest ONLY when a line is
   stated - no cached path of a document without one goes stale.

## The readings

- The WCS origin is the stated line's anchor: the post subtracts the
  work offset from world coordinates, so in program coordinates the
  rotary centreline passes through the WCS origin - the same law the
  index-swing clause and the lathe spindle law read.
- The judge is the fit's own (`axis.rs`'s `data_of` + `judge`): the
  tolerance, the 90% concurrency share, the coarseness skip and the
  bearing law, evaluated about the stated line instead of a candidate
  from the eigen search. On the reporter's helical rotor the judge
  fails and the radial raster stays LOCKED (the decision doc's law:
  its radial pose can gouge on helical lobes) - the disagreement
  refusal says so and names the 4-axis case.
- A machine whose work-turning rotary states no `axis` vector keeps
  today's fit (absent is not stated, never zero). A trunnion's
  work-turning pair is read in chain order and the first line the
  model holds wins, so a standing revolve takes the C and a lying
  one takes the A.

## Pinning tests

- motion `axis_stated_tests`: a revolve holds its stated line and
  reads the fitted axis bit for bit; the canonical line is signed
  and pinned; a stated line away from the part names the part's own
  axis; the helical screw refuses with the 4-axis wording; an empty
  mesh refuses like the fit.
- app `rotary_stated_axis`:
  `a_stated_machine_line_generates_the_fitted_path` (microARC 4 +
  laid revolve: move-for-move the fitted program),
  `the_millturns_stated_c_carries_the_standing_bar` (C answered
  without a fit, the stamp runs),
  `the_screw_rotor_on_a_stated_A_is_refused_by_name` (the radial
  kinds stay locked on the screw),
  `the_screw_rotor_without_a_stated_line_keeps_the_old_refusal`
  (the pinned "share no rotation axis" words untouched),
  `a_stated_line_away_from_the_part_names_the_parts_own_axis` (both
  the disagreement and the letter-door wordings),
  `a_stated_line_the_part_holds_on_a_machine_that_has_it_generates`
  (the op's own statement, either sign),
  `a_work_offset_move_moves_the_stated_line_and_refuses` (the
  anchor is the WCS's own position),
  `the_stated_axis_round_trips_the_project_file` (v78 round-trip,
  v77 steps up unstated),
  `a_v77_file_opens_and_a_newer_file_is_refused` (the version pin).
- app `rotary_gate`: `a_stated_line_answers_the_letter_without_a_fit`
  (the screw's fit refuses, the stated line still answers).
- app `rotary_field_parity`:
  `the_stated_axis_parallel_reads_the_radial_law` - the heavy-lane
  parity of the stated-A program (the field eye vs the radial law,
  `#[ignore]`d like its three siblings; the quick suite pins the
  path equality, this lane proves the stated axis flows the whole
  sim pipeline at the verdict class).
- The continuous 4-axis example regenerated at v78 (its op follows
  the microARC's stated line - the same path the fit reads).

## What was NOT exercised

- The heavy parity lane runs at a cut, not here (the quick gate
  pins the path equality instead).
- No UI pixel snapshot is touched (release-lane only).

## Not included (the issue stays open)

- The RADIAL DROP FINISH KERNEL and the radial-step roughing
  (decision part 3/4): the live claim on
  `mkinney:issue/2772-radial-drop` holds that work. This PR's
  disagreement refusal keeps the radial kinds locked on helical
  parts until that kernel can consume the stated axis safely.
- No 360-degree radial drop finish for Rotary Parallel, no
  Doosan/Fanuc posting of one - same slice.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read a
stated rotation axis first (the operation's own direction, else the
machine's stated rotary line through the work offset origin), judged
against the model's faces - a part on the stated line cuts the fitted
path unchanged, a part whose faces disagree refuses by name (the
4-axis case named), and nothing stated keeps the fitted axis (v78
project files).

title: feat(multiaxis): Rotary Flow kernel - flow lines between picked helical guide chains
body:
## What changed

The first slice of the Rotary Flow kind (issue #2824, part of #2804): a 4-axis cylindrical flow-line kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`, split over four files under the 400-line law.

- `rotary_flow.rs` - the public entry. `rotary_flow(chains, facets, ax, p, c)` takes the picked guide chains, the part facets, the STATED rotation axis (the #2772 seam - the axis is a parameter, never fitted here), `RotaryFlowParams` and `AxisControl`. The params carry the `Tool` itself, so the ball-nose requirement is refused by name. Clearance and retract read as ball-center radii about the axis.
- `rotary_flow_unwrap.rs` - each chain unwound to a continuous `(theta, v)` track (the radian twin of `cl::unwrap_near`), each adjacent pair aligned by the nearest whole turn, the band developed `(s = R_ref * theta, v)` with `R_ref` the chains' outermost radius, and the picked-chain ground checks (finite, distinct, on-model, off-axis).
- `rotary_flow_pass.rs` - the iso-parametric flow curves between the aligned pair, each station's ball center pushed out along its radial until the `closest_pt_tri` oracle clears every facet (march, then bisect), the curve chorded within `min(ARC_FIT_TOL, tolerance)` over the union of the two chains' arc-length knots.
- `rotary_flow_emit.rs` - tips via the pivot law (`retip`), cut poses through the lean law on the radial (`tilt`), links rebuilt radially on the retract cylinders (`rotary_links`' law: feed retract, chorded index short way round, radial plunge), the program opening on the clearance pose (M13.8).

Refusals by name: a tool that is not a ball-nose, fewer than two chains, a non-finite point, a point off the model, a point on the axis line, chains wound in opposite senses, a band with no width, a stepover or tolerance at the scallop ceiling (the finishing kinds' own law), a station the push-out cannot clear within five radii, a pass count over the 4096-pass ceiling, a clearance that does not clear the work.

The decisions taken unattended are in `docs/decisions/2824-rotary-flow-kernel.md`: the `Tool`-carrying params (the drilling precedent), the ball-center radius reading of the heights, `R_ref` at the chains' outermost radius (ground inside it gets finer, never coarser), and one band per adjacent chain pair with both edge passes kept (a shared middle chain is walked once per band - the re-cut is the same geometry at the same depth).

## The readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 29 steps, 0 failed - motion lib, `multiaxis`, `rotary`, the new `rotary_flow` binary, and the reached app suites (operations, posed_contact, rotary_fixtures, rotary_verify, and the rest). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- On the rotor groove fixture: the developed band reads 4.000 mm at R 8.000 mm; 6 flow passes at a 0.9 mm stepover; the first pass rides the wall push-out (rho about 11), interior passes ride the floor a ball radius off it; every cut station's ball keeps its radius off the part.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow/rotary_flow_tests.rs` (15 tests): every refusal by name (non-ball tool, chain count, empty model, off-model at its spot, on-axis, degenerate band, opposite senses, both scallop ceilings, low clearance), the pass count law, `align_pair`'s nearest whole turn, `lerp_at`, `unwrap_near`, and a small on-model band that poses, clears and opens at clearance.
- `crates/motion/tests/rotary_flow.rs` (3 run, 1 heavy): `a_rotor_floor_band_flows_multi_turn_without_gouge` (the no-gouge pin over every station against `camcraft_sim`'s own `dist_seg_tri`, multi-turn span, wall vs floor riders), `a_pair_straddling_the_branch_aligns_by_a_whole_turn` (same pass count as the unshifted band, the note stating the shift), `climb_reverses_each_pass`, and the ignored `the_rotor_envelope_stays_gouge_free_at_the_scallop_law` (heavy lane: release --ignored, the 4-turn fine rotor envelope scanned station by station).

## What was not exercised

- The app layer, the command and the MCP tool are owed to the #2804 sub-issues; this PR changes only the motion kernel.
- The whole-turn alignment is pinned by the kernel basis' own branch (e1 = +Y on a Z axis); a pair straddling a different frame's branch reaches the same law through the same shift.
- A band whose pair meets at a whole-turn boundary exactly (offset = half a lap) is not tested; the nearest-turn law would pick either side.
- `graphify update` did not run: the `graphify` command is not on this session's PATH.
- Heavy lane: only the ignored envelope scan touches it; it runs at the cut.

Changelog: multiaxis: Rotary Flow - a 4-axis flow-line finishing kernel between picked helical guide chains on a stated rotation axis

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- Skims on an open run are not judged per pass by the wire verify (it
  refuses them by name); a follow-up can split the passes and judge
  each at its own kerf.
- Taper, burnout and 4-axis cuts do not read the overlap; each refuses
  an open run or walks the closed lap as before.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

title: feat: open a project read-only with --read-only and open_project read_only
body:
## What changed

`camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens a project read-only. The MCP
tool `open_project` takes `read_only: true` for the same result. A save
over the opened file is then refused on every save route, and the file
stays byte for byte. A save to another file works and ends read-only. The
title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.

- One rule, `project::refuse_read_only_save` in `crates/app/src/project/`,
  refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The
  window's `State::save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it.
  `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP
  seam of a window.
- The rule compares canonical paths, so a save from the Save As dialog
  to the opened file is refused too.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as
  the editor for shipped machines does. The Save of the unsaved-changes
  prompt does the same.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- The read-only state is kept next to the document path:
  `State::project_read_only` in the window, `Env::doc_read_only` in a
  headless MCP session or a script run. The live seam gets the window's
  state through `LiveOptions::read_only`.
- A model file with `--read-only` is imported as usual. A headless start
  ignores the option. The live seam still refuses `open_project`.
- The same option name and behaviour as the open SolidCraft proposal
  for `--read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830).
- No change to the file format or `PROJECT_VERSION`.
- Docs: the `--help` text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`,
  `site/content/guide/automate/cli.md` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3609-read-only-open.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `60b19abe8`. Two merges of upstream
main follow it: `b94dcd378` (main `82db54282`) and `98cd5b28b` (main
`3fc0e017b`). There is no rebase.

- The first merge had conflicts with #3608 (overwrite guard) and #3584
  (start options). Both sides added lines in the same places. The merge
  keeps both sides.
- In `v_save` and `State::save_project_path`, the read-only check runs
  first, and then the overwrite guard of #3608. Thus `overwrite: true`
  does not write over a file that is open read-only.
- `--read-only` comes after `--no-activate` and `--minimized` in the
  options table, the `--help` text and `start-options.md`.
  `run_windowed` takes the start mode and `read_only`.
- `LiveOptions` and `Env` have `read_only` and `doc_stamp`. The
  `save_project` description has the sentences of both changes.
- `crates/app/tests/save_overwrite_guard.rs` gets one line,
  `read_only: false`, in its `LiveOptions` value. This is the only line
  outside the files of this change.
- The second merge had no conflicts. It brings in #3687 (a relative
  model link resolves against the project folder).

## Tests

title: fix(project): ask or refuse before a save writes over a changed project file
body:
## What changed

A save to the project's own file now checks the file on disk first. The
project remembers the file's disk stamp (path, size, modification time)
when it is opened and after each save. If the stamp is different at the
next save, the file on disk changed after the open or the last save:

- The window holds the save and asks: **Save As**, **Cancel** or
  **Overwrite**. Nothing is written before the answer.
- `cam.save` and the MCP tool `save_project` refuse by name. The refusal
  names the file and `overwrite: true`. `save_project` has a new optional
  argument `overwrite`. `cam.save` has a new options object:
  `cam.save(path?, { overwrite?: boolean })`.
- An agent attached to the window uses the window's stamp. The live seam
  takes it in (`LiveOptions::doc_stamp`) and gives the new stamp back
  (`LiveAnswer::doc_stamp`), so the window does not ask about the
  agent's own save.

A save to another path, a new document and a file that was deleted are
not checked. The stamp of our own save replaces the old stamp, so the
next save does not ask. In the window, New and Open drop the old stamp
and a held save, so a held save never writes another document.

- The stamp is `project::DiskStamp`, beside `project::save` and
  `project::load`. The checks are `script::save_guard::check` and
  `State::may_save_over`.
  `project::save`, the file format and `PROJECT_VERSION` do not change.
- Behaviour change: a script or an agent that saved over a changed file
  is now refused. It must pass `overwrite: true`.
- The behaviour matches SolidCraft's overwrite guard. The texts are
  CamCraft's own.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` are updated for
  the new argument. The MCP and CLI guide pages have one paragraph each.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3608-save-overwrite-guard.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `60b19abe8`.

## Tests

New in `crates/app/tests/save_overwrite_guard.rs`:

- `a_stamp_sees_a_foreign_write_but_not_a_missing_file_or_another_path`
- `an_mcp_save_over_a_changed_file_is_refused_until_overwrite`
- `an_mcp_open_stamps_the_file`
- `a_save_to_another_path_or_over_a_deleted_file_is_not_refused`
- `a_bad_save_option_is_refused_by_name_and_writes_nothing`
- `a_script_save_over_a_changed_file_is_refused_until_overwrite`
- `an_attached_agent_save_meets_the_window_stamp_and_hands_back_the_new_one`

New in `crates/ui/src/save_guard_tests.rs`:

- `a_save_over_a_changed_file_asks_and_overwrite_replaces_it`
- `cancel_keeps_the_file_and_save_as_goes_to_the_save_as_dialog`
- `the_window_s_own_saves_never_ask`
- `a_save_to_another_file_or_over_a_deleted_file_does_not_ask`
- `a_held_save_from_the_unsaved_prompt_keeps_the_document_open`
- `a_new_document_drops_a_held_save`

New layout test: `layout_window_overwrite_prompt`
(`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/page_layout_windows.rs`).

`cargo xtask gate quick` (Windows 11): 216 steps, 214 passed, 2 failed,
0 stalled. It ran the app and ui libs (ui lib: 1480 passed, the new tests
and the layout test among them), `save_overwrite_guard` (7 passed),
`mcp_live`, `mcp_doc_drift`, `scripting`, every app suite that names
`app::project`, `app::script` or `mcp (tools)`, and 16 ui suites.
The 2 failed steps do not touch this change:

- `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`
  fails on upstream/main `60b19abe8` (#3574, main is red).
- `example_catalog::catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::{rebuilds,regenerates}`
  differs only by line ends: this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf=true`)
  turns the LF file `examples/catalog/2d/drill-overfeed/refusal.txt`
  into CRLF.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
The gate and clippy ran on this change before the issue existed. The head
differs from that tree only in the issue number: in code comments and in
the name of the decision file.
Heavy lanes: not run. The change is not under the safety floor (no
posted G-code, collision check, simulation or geometry), so no targeted
heavy step applies (#3556).
Reach from `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run`: "app heavy: every target"
(212 steps), because `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs` changed. Not run.

## Not exercised

- The window's step that keeps an agent's new stamp (`mcp_host.rs`, three
  lines). The app test pins the stamp that the live seam gives back. The
  AI chat's Allow path is not driven in a test.
- The prompt's buttons by a click. The tests call
  `actions::resolve_overwrite`, and the layout test checks the modal.
- Save As after the prompt: it opens the system file dialog. The test
  checks that the Save As command is queued.
- A write that keeps the size and the modification time. Some file systems
  keep the time in steps of 1 or 2 seconds. This is a known limit.
- Two real CamCraft processes, git, a sync client and a network share. A
  plain write of other bytes stands in for each.
- Linux and macOS.

title: fix(2d): note the corner reliefs that get no spur
body:
## What changed

A planned corner relief whose start no pass vertex reaches, and for which no legal detour exists, was dropped without a diagnostic (#3249). It could leave material the operator does not expect.

- `inject_relief_spurs` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs`) now reports each skipped relief: the caller gets the boundary corners in a `misses` vector.
- The pocket emit path (`pocket_emit.rs`) and the pocket avoid path (`pocket_avoid.rs`) write one note per corner into the `PathBuilder` / path notes: `corner relief at (x, y) is not cut: no pass vertex reaches the relief spur`. Notes are de-duplicated by corner, so a multi-level cut or a retry names each corner once.
- The four-dogbones rest test keeps its no-note assert: a reached relief adds no note.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket corner relief that no pass reaches is now named in the operation notes instead of being dropped silently.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::corner_relief_spur::tests::a_relief_no_pass_reaches_is_reported_as_a_miss` (crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs): the miss is reported and no spur is spliced in; a reached relief reports no miss and gets its spur.
- `unreachable_corners_and_bad_overrides_are_refused` (crates/motion/tests/corner_relief.rs): the island-blocked spur refuses at plan time.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_corner_relief.rs`: the rest pass keeps its no-note assert.

## Review fix

The miss vector uses `r.corner`, the boundary corner, instead of `r.start`, the cutter-center start.
Both existing callers use the returned corners for duplicate detection.

- The existing miss pin now uses corner `(0,0)` and start `(3,3)`.
- `machining2d::pocket_emit::tests::missed_relief_notes_name_and_deduplicate_boundary_corners` checks the resulting path notes.
  It checks equal corners with different starts and different corners with an equal start.

## Review fix validation

Final head: `1814e1119b8fdbf86f1f6a4fe8b245b9a30286e0`.
Base: `9dfcc7ac2ae59c30a43796382968b4cba93970e5` (`upstream/main`).

The actual runs used base `9dfcc7ac2ae59c30a43796382968b4cba93970e5`. A merge with newer main was not exercised.

The miss vector now contains boundary corners. Existing callers use these points to remove duplicate notes.
The path-note test checks equal corners with different starts and different corners with an equal start.

Pin proof:

- `machining2d::corner_relief_spur::tests::a_relief_no_pass_reaches_is_reported_as_a_miss`
- `machining2d::pocket_emit::tests::missed_relief_notes_name_and_deduplicate_boundary_corners`

Each pin passed with the fix. Changing `misses.push(r.corner)` back to `misses.push(r.start)` made both pins fail.
The first pin reported `(3,3)` instead of `(0,0)`. The path-note pin reported `(3,3)` and `(4,3)` instead of `(0,0)` and `(10,0)`.
Restoring the fix made both pins pass again. Commands used `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib <full_test_name> -- --exact`.

title: feat(motion): engrave and trace open and closed sketch chains
body:
Engrave and Trace now follow open and closed chains from a placed sketch. The user can select a profile, individual chains or a layer. The operation preserves the cut direction of lines, arcs and circles. It applies the sketch placement and the work-coordinate rotation to both endpoints and arc centers. A lift separates disconnected strokes and gaps accepted by the drawing tolerance.

Each depth level approaches from the stock surface. The existing stock, fixture, shank and mark-depth checks can hold the post, including jobs that have no part solid. Very short arcs below the post resolution give a diagnostic. A major arc is split into two arcs that keep its center and sweep. #3442 tracks the separate case where a native Fanuc post accepts a short arc supplied directly in an intermediate file.

The 18-move CL fixture contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes.

## Goldens moved

No existing golden moves. One new recorded file is added.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/sketch_engrave_trace.cl` (NEW, not moved)

The new CL file records 18 moves. It contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes. The test `placed_sketch_marks_keep_open_and_closed_arcs_and_retract_between_strokes` compares the generated moves with this file.

## Verification

- On the parent source, `placed_sketch_marks_keep_open_and_closed_arcs_and_retract_between_strokes` failed because an operation could not use picked sketch chains. The same test passed on this fix. The original CLI also refused both Engrave and Trace on a whole profile.
- On `2032dda7e`, all 11 feature tests passed. The 18 moves matched the checked-in golden. The stock depth, underside, stock rapid, crossing and fixture checks held the post when required. Project round-trip and MCP passed.
- `short_and_near_full_arcs_keep_their_center_and_sweep_through_a_rotated_work_offset` checks the arc centers and sweeps. The native CLI generated, verified and posted six synthetic drawings across both operations. Short representable arcs kept distinct endpoints. The 270-degree and near-full sweeps used split arcs with the correct centers. Both sub-resolution cases gave a named refusal and wrote no NC file.
- The focused gate passed 480 app tests, 127 post tests, and 29 motion tests on the final commit. Strict Clippy passed for all app, motion, and post targets with warnings denied. A broader motion run passed 646 tests with 10 ignored on the earlier branch revision with identical motion source.
- The broad quick plan was a dry run. The focused app, motion and post suites and strict Clippy ran on this head. All 243 selected release-mode execution steps completed. They recorded 105 passing ignored tests and 4 registered expected failures. Of the selected steps, 206 had no ignored cases to run. Each selected suite compiled on demand. The separate aggregate compile-only step was omitted.

The CLI checks used synthetic drawings and the native post. No physical machine ran the resulting programs.

## Review gates on head c7048825c (after the second merge of main)

- Merge base: `origin/main` `3c68dcaf2`. Merge commit: `173abf61b`.
- Hand-resolved hunk: `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, the Trace and Engrave arm.
  - Main (#3349) split the Engrave arm to plan with `machining2d::trace_avoid` when a "Do not touch" spec is set.
  - This PR joins the Trace and Engrave arms and adds the sketch-stroke path.
  - The resolution keeps both. A sketch pick rides its strokes (`strokes.trace`). A model pick runs `trace_avoid` for Engrave with a spec, and the plain `trace` for Trace, as on main.
- New commit `c7048825c` `fix(app): judge sketch Engrave strokes against Do not touch`:
  - `trace_avoid` takes closed loops only, so it cannot plan around open sketch strokes.
  - The final path of a sketch Engrave now goes through `avoid::protect_path`, as a Trace does. Links are lifted, and a stroke that meets a protected item is refused by name.
  - A sketch Trace already went through `protect_path` on main. The post gate (`live_avoid_problems`) applies to both.
- Pinning test: `sketch_engrave_trace::avoid::do_not_touch_refuses_a_sketch_stroke_that_passes_too_near_a_protected_face` (Trace and Engrave). A mutation that removes the sketch Engrave judgement makes it fail.
- Targeted runs: `sketch_engrave_trace` 12 passed; `do_not_touch` 7 passed (main's Trace avoidance tests); `do_not_touch_engrave` 3 passed.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 855 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled. 8,112 tests passed, 1 failed, 135 ignored.
  - The red step is `app suites: rotary_verify`, `a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius` (2,110 moves, pinned 2,064). Main was red there at the merge base (#3774). Main fixed it in `473600714` after the merge. This PR does not touch the rotary code or the test.
- `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: in the quick plan, 41 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Delta class (`cargo xtask merge-plan --delta 3458 --reviewed e42e54249`): NEW CODE. `173abf61` is a merge of main, HAND-RESOLVED in `generate.rs`; `c7048825` is a new commit.

## Review gates on head e42e54249 (after the merge of main)
