title: feat(chamfer): select a tip offset
body:
## What changed

2D Chamfer has a `Tip offset` setting. A positive offset moves the cone axis toward physical air and lowers its virtual tip by `(tip offset + chamfer width) * tan(angle)`. The selected cone band runs from the tip offset to the tip offset plus chamfer width. The declared `EdgeBreak` stays on the original selected edge with the authored width and depth.

Closed loops and selected open chains support the setting. Generation refuses a wrong Side, material crossing, excessive tool radius or flute reach, and an offset that folds or loses any selected boundary span. The partial-collapse refusal covers a narrow branch disappearing while its parent loop survives. Zero offset preserves the complete legacy closed and open `Toolpath`, including floating-point depth bytes.

The parameter reaches the UI, commands, stamps, project files, and MCP create/edit/read/save/reset. The UI shows the control and derived virtual-tip height. The persisted field remains `minimum_cone_radius`.

## Breaking project-format change

Project format **v79** cannot be opened by v78 readers. The fix commit records the existing format break with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Migration preserves the legacy zero offset; project round trips preserve positive values.

## Review fixes

1. Check every original boundary span after a positive offset; loop count alone is insufficient.
2. Restore the exact legacy depth calculation on both zero-offset routes. Compare complete results with captured pre-feature paths.
3. Add before/after control and height-note screenshots below.
4. Record the reason for each retained test binary below.
5. Record the format break and correct the body to v79.

## Test binary placement

These PR binaries remain separate for this fix round. They are not isolated-suite exemptions.

- `crates/motion/tests/chamfer_minimum_radius.rs`: keep the complete closed/open cone-band geometry and refusal fixture in the lowest owning crate, independently runnable from application tests.

- `crates/app/tests/mcp_chamfer_minimum_radius.rs`: keep the JSON-RPC create/patch/read/save/reset round trip together with its single isolated server fixture.

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

The SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads drawings into the DXF `Document` type. It shares sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, sketch entities, and project storage with DXF import.

- Read paths, lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles, and ellipses.
- Apply group transforms and references to elements in the same file.
- Keep circular arcs analytic. Flatten Beziers and other ellipses within 0.005 mm.
- Read mm, cm, in, pt, pc, and px sizes, `viewBox`, and `preserveAspectRatio`.
- Reflect Y about the page height. Use top-level group labels or IDs as layers.
- Count unsupported content, hidden content, markers and paint-only stylesheets as skipped. This includes stylesheets inside `<defs>`.
- Add the undoable `ImportSvg` command, the `import_svg` MCP tool, and the `cam.importSvg` script verb.
- Update the user guide and MCP reference. Record decisions in `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals

The reader names malformed input, unsupported units, invalid sizes, singular transforms, and exceeded import limits. A file without physical units needs the caller's unit. A sized file refuses a caller unit.

The reader also refuses root `<svg>` transform attributes, and `transform-origin` and `transform-box` presentation attributes.

The reader finds a duplicate attribute name with a map. The scan that it replaces was quadratic in the attribute count of one tag.

The reader reads an inline `style` against an allow-list of the properties that cannot change geometry (`SAFE_PROPERTIES` in `svg/facts.rs`). The reader refuses each other property by name. The reader reads the style and the transform of an element one time, finds a `use` target in a map of the ids, and charges the shape data of each visit against a work budget.

These rules close the class "an input changes or hides a shape, and the import ignores it":

- A `<style>` sheet is checked with the same allow-list, with no selector matching (`svg/sheet.rs`). The reader refuses `display`, `visibility` and each property that is not on the list. A paint-only sheet imports.
- The reader refuses an `<?xml-stylesheet?>` instruction and a `<link rel="stylesheet">` by name.
- The reader refuses `animate`, `set`, `animateTransform`, `animateMotion`, `animateColor` and `discard` at each place in the tree.
- A child of a shape or of a `use` that is not `title`, `desc`, `metadata` or `style` is counted as `<child> in <parent>`.
- The reader refuses a `preserveAspectRatio` value that is not in the SVG grammar.
- A marker property that draws a marker is counted as `marker`.
- The user guide says that a shape with a stroke imports as its centre line.

## The fix round for the review on `f96ea8fa0`

1. **One CSS scanner for the inline style and the sheet (`svg/css.rs`, new).** `sheet.rs` and `style.rs` take their pieces from it, so the two cannot split a style at different places.
   - An unquoted `url(` token ends at the first `)` that is not escaped, as in CSS Syntax 3 (4.3.6). In it, a quote starts no string, a `(` adds no level, and a `;`, a brace or a `/*` starts nothing.
   - `url` is found in any case and through escapes (`\75rl(`). `url(` before a quote is a function with a string, and the usual rules apply.
   - A bad url token (a quote, a `(` or a gap in the address) is refused by name: in a sheet at each place (a rule, an `@font-face` block, a prelude), and in the inline style of an imported element.
   - If the same inline style has `display:none`, the shape is hidden as in a browser. Nothing of it is imported, and it is counted as `hidden`.
2. **One function for references (`svg/reference.rs`, new).** After an `&`, the run goes to the first `;`, white space, `&`, `<` or quote. A run that ends at a `;` is a reference.
   - A reference is decoded only if it is one of the five predefined entities, or a character reference to a character that XML permits. The count of leading zeros has no limit.
   - Each other reference is refused by name: an entity name with a character outside ASCII, a run that is not an XML name (`&a=b;`, `A`), a code point that is not a character (`�`, `�`).
   - The namespace exception stays: the value of `xmlns` and `xmlns:*` is not read. A CDATA section has no references.
   - The scan is linear: the next search starts after the run.
3. **Directory suites.** This PR adds no new top-level test binary to a crate that has a directory suite for it.
   - `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` is now `crates/app/tests/mcp/svg.rs`, a module of the existing `mcp` suite. Its 2 tests are the same.
   - The four files `svg_refusals.rs`, `svg_style_safety.rs`, `svg_tree_rules.rs` and `svg_visibility.rs` are now modules in `crates/geometry/tests/svg/`. The two new pin files are there too.
   - New top-level test file: `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs`. Reason: `crates/geometry/tests/` had no directory suite for the SVG reader, and this file is the root of the new one (one binary in place of five).
   - `#[test]` count of the SVG suite: 61 before (16 + 19 + 6 + 9 + 11), 74 now. The 13 more are the new pins.

One existing pin changed its expected text. `.a{fill:url(a}b);transform:scale(2)}` was refused as "style sheet has a ';' outside a rule". The scanner now reads the `}` as a part of the address, and the reader refuses the file as "style sheet transform".

## Validation on the final head

Head: `ccb0ed35486a1689323753d5efc0b757b959fa39`. It has one commit after `245e84fa1`: a merge of `upstream/main` `074c23ba6`. The head `245e84fa1` had no review, thus this push has no review finding.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 1,190 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled, 20.5 minutes. The red step is `app suites: rotary_verify`; see below |
| `clippy -D warnings` | PASS: a step of the quick gate |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | PASS: 98 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 17.8 minutes |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | PASS in the quick gate |
| `app suites: mcp` (has `mcp/svg.rs`), `mcp_doc_drift` | PASS in the quick gate |
| `geometry suites: svg` | PASS in the quick gate |

**The red step is the red step of main.** `rotary_verify::a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius` fails (2110 moves, expected 2064). Issue #3774 records the same failure of the post-merge gate on main `074c23ba6`. This PR changes no rotary, motion or sim file. This PR does not correct it.

**Merge of main.** The merge `ccb0ed354` had one conflict.

- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (a generated file). I wrote it again with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- mcp reference`. It has 124 tools: the 123 tools of main and `import_svg`.
- The merge has no other hand edit. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is the file of main.

Main moved to `f6716cdcd` during the gates. `git merge-tree` of this head with that main is clean. The gates did not run against that main.

The gate light did not run again in this round. The earlier merge `3178256d7` (main `6167d30af`) and its gates are in the PR comments.

**Pin proof.** (From the round on `245e84fa1`; the merge changes no code of this PR, and I did not run the mutations again.) For each row, I made the mutation, ran `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test svg`, and restored the code. With the code restored, all 74 tests pass.

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| The scanner does not read `url(` tokens (`css.rs`: the `url(` arm is off). This is the behaviour before the fix. | `url_tokens::svg_style_sheet_bad_url_tokens_are_refused_by_name`, `url_tokens::svg_font_face_block_with_a_bad_url_token_is_refused_by_name`, `url_tokens::svg_inline_bad_url_tokens_are_refused_by_name_on_a_shape_a_group_and_the_root`, `url_tokens::svg_inline_display_none_after_a_bad_url_token_hides_the_shape`, `url_tokens::svg_a_comment_start_in_a_url_token_hides_no_declaration`, `url_tokens::svg_good_url_tokens_import_at_the_attribute_size`, `tree_rules::svg_style_sheet_rules_that_hide_or_resize_a_shape_are_refused_by_name` |
| A reference that is not a character stays as text, and a character reference with more than 9 digits is not decoded (`reference.rs`). This is the behaviour before the fix. | `references::svg_entity_names_outside_ascii_are_refused_at_each_place`, `references::svg_a_run_that_is_not_an_xml_name_is_refused_when_it_ends_at_a_semicolon`, `references::svg_character_references_with_leading_zeros_are_decoded_in_an_attribute`, `references::svg_character_references_with_leading_zeros_are_decoded_in_a_style_sheet`, `references::svg_character_references_that_are_not_a_character_are_refused_by_name`, `tree_rules::svg_doctype_entity_references_are_refused_by_name` |

These pins stay green in the two mutations, because they pin what must still import: `references::svg_predefined_and_plain_references_read_as_before`, `references::svg_many_reference_starts_read_in_linear_time`, and the usual `url(data:font/woff2;base64,AAAA)` rule in `tree_rules::svg_paint_only_style_sheets_import_at_the_attribute_size`.

The pins of the earlier rounds are in `tests/svg/tree_rules.rs`, `style_safety.rs`, `refusals.rs` and `visibility.rs`. Their mutation table is in the review record of `671426992`. I did not run those mutations again in this round.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog suites ran and passed on the final head. The diff against `upstream/main` changes no recorded program, golden or snapshot PNG.

## Not exercised

- I did not check the url and reference cases in a browser. The expected results are from CSS Syntax 3 and XML 1.0.
- The three follow-ups of the review on `f96ea8fa0` are not in this round: `<!ATTLIST` defaults of the DOCTYPE (`P3`), `systemLanguage` and `requiredExtensions` (`P3`), and a count of `<script>` and event attributes (`P7`). The review says to file them after the merge.
- A sheet scan does not follow `(` and `[` levels across a `}`. I examined this, and each case that I found is refused, not imported. It has no pin of its own.
- A posted G-code golden for an SVG profile remains in follow-up #3042.
- The `import_svg` row in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` remains outside this PR.
- Nested SVG viewports, selector matching of a style sheet, text to outlines, and embedded images remain outside this reader's scope.
- The merge with main `f6716cdcd` is not built and not gated. The merged main is `074c23ba6`.
- The description of the `import_svg` MCP tool is not changed.
- The four follow-ups of the first review on `eaafd2e72` (Inkscape long style, `vector-effect` attribute, the 5 s time limits, the skill row) are not changed.

No UI source changed. Before/after screenshots do not apply.

title: feat(wire): group up to nine captured punches on one plate
body:
Stacked on #2981. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1e12c77a4150252c34df3f23fc2ff1c85fe2e3fa...13c98065810173c6da65264cfa6799df470d5cd6).

This PR is ported onto the zero-step setup frame of #2984 and the stack up to #2981. The old writer of this PR is gone. The old head was `c81cfd1d4`.

## What changed

- A punch group holds 2 to 9 complete modeled punches on one 20 mm plate. The limit is `agie_setup::MAX_PUNCH_WORKS` (9). It applies in these three places:
  - `PunchGroup20::encode` (was `GROUP_WORKS = 2`);
  - `agie::export_group_with_review` (was `jobs.len() != 2`);
  - the app dispatch in `posting_agie.rs` (was `1..=2`).
- Each work has its own ISO (`<group>1.ISO` to `<group>9.ISO`), its own SBR line, its own work `CUTn` and its own threading hole. All works refer to the ONE `CCB030` quality object of the piece (#2984). The old PR body said "each work gets its own resident quality object". This port does not do that, because #2984 showed that different quality names can bind to different resident data.
- The clear-band check compares every pair of works, not only neighbours in the program. The message names the two works, for example `The works TRIO201 and TRIO203 share a cutting area`.
- A punch group refuses a placed drawing, as a die group does.
- Die groups stay at two openings. The PR has no control evidence for larger die groups. `encode_die`, the post and the app refuse a third opening with their own message.
- New messages: `SetupError::GroupWorks`, the post group refusal and the app count refusal state the new limits.
- New examples `examples/agie/punch-trio.camscript` and `punch-grid.camscript`. They use the post name `Native wire EDM job files`.
- The user guide section is now **Group captured punches**.

## Value sources

No new control value. The 20 mm offsets (245, 155, 140 and 134 µm), the TECCUT row and all SBL fields are those of the checked pair `PAIR20` (#2961). Only the work name, the resource and the hole change for each work. The stock (120 × 100 × 20 mm), the 32 mm pitch, the 14 × 16 mm punch (`pair-left.obj`) and the holes 13 mm left of each centre are from the examples of this PR.

## Readings

Emulated Classic Cut 2S, 2026-11-24, throwaway clone of the practice image (base SHA-256 unchanged, clone deleted). The files of this frame were imported, and the bytes on the guest disk were identical.

| | TRIO20 (3 works) | NINE20 (9 works) |
|---|---|---|
| After import | `CCB030[0]`, own `stp1` and ISO on each work | same, 9 distinct resources |
| Quality on each work | CCB030 Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0, Te 1.5, options off | same, also on CUT9 |
| TECCUT | row 0199, `estbca25nnn060b030020`, T100 on each work (20 mm row) | same |
| After TECCUT | `CCB030[4]` on each work | same |
| FORMALCHECK | `geen fouten`; warnings `Uitgekozen opties : 131072`, `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` | same |
| J00 cut blocks | 24 | 72 |
| Cut order | profile passes of CUT1..CUT3, then the 1.000 mm separations | profile passes of CUT1..CUT9, then the separations |
| Transits between works | head up (Z53 or Z80) only | same, 37 moves, none below Z53 |
| Cutting envelopes | 3 pairs, 0 overlap | 36 pairs, 0 overlap |

The quality problem of the old run (the first and the ninth generic quality names bound to different resident targets) does not occur: there is only one quality object.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib: `group_count_tests::every_group_size_has_its_own_file_work_and_hole_and_one_quality`, `a_tenth_punch_or_a_third_die_opening_writes_nothing`, `a_collision_of_works_that_are_not_neighbours_names_the_pair`; `group_tests::a_group_refuses_a_die_two_works_on_one_area_another_stock_or_no_separation` (updated).
- `camcraft-post` `agie_group_setup`: `trio_and_grid_files_match_their_goldens_with_one_quality` (new goldens `TRIO20.SBL/SBR`, `NINE20.SBL/SBR`), `a_group_refuses_its_unqualified_inputs` (ten works); `agie_die_group_setup`: three distinct openings refused.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native`: `group::three_model_owners_post_the_trio_goldens` (ISO goldens `TRIO201..203.ISO`), `group::nine_model_owners_post_the_grid_goldens_with_their_own_iso_and_hole`, `group::a_tenth_work_an_unowned_model_a_shared_source_or_a_far_collision_writes_nothing`, `die_group::a_missing_shared_or_unsafe_die_work_writes_nothing` (three die works).
- Unchanged bytes: the PAIR20, DUODI20, CCSEP20, DIE20, LOWER20, RACE20, CIRCLE20, FINE20 and inspection goldens are not edited, and their tests pass.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on `13c980658` (the stack touches geometry, so quick falls back to batch): 1193 steps, 1192 ok, 0 stalled. The step `clippy -D warnings` (geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, gpu, ui, all targets) passed. The one red step is `app suites: rotary_verify` (`a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius`). That is the known red main of #3774 on the stack base; this PR does not touch that code. No heavy lane, by AGENTS.md (`P6`).

## Not exercised

- No physical cut.
- A tenth work, mixed punch and die groups, and die groups of more than two openings: refused, no control run.
- Nested or diagonal layouts that a box check refuses although they are safe.

Changelog: The native wire EDM post accepts groups of up to nine captured punches on one 20 mm plate. It checks the cutting areas of every pair of works and names the two works that meet. All works use one quality object.

Fixes #2980

title: feat(wire): group two die openings of one retained plate
body:
Stacked on #2979. Review the [die pair changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/17cb6f617460627b543f160f0e06821a752bac27...1e12c77a4150252c34df3f23fc2ff1c85fe2e3fa).

Process change: yes

This PR is ported onto the zero-step setup of #2984. The quality-binding correction of #2984 now applies to the die pair: the piece has one CCB030 quality object, and both works refer to it. The old writer (`jescript.rs`) is gone. The PR ports the behaviour, not the old writer.

## What changed

- **App.** Two Wire Contour operations with the die side make a die group. Each operation selects the upper rim of one through-opening of the same modeled plate. The plate must be the only model, with no placed drawing. The plate must have exactly two through-openings, one for each operation. Each selected rim must match the full-height opening of the plate (`operation/agie_die.rs`). A single die job keeps its check and its message (exactly one through-opening).
- **Post.** `export_group_with_review` accepts two die openings as well as two punches. Both works must have the same side. A punch and a die in one group are refused. Each opening gets the existing die checks of #2957 (20 mm plate, convex opening, hole inside the opening, inward lead, reach and stock margin). The clear band check now covers die openings: the cutting area of each work holds the opening, its hole and 3 mm lead, the rough corner and the wire radius. The same opening selected twice fails this check.
- **Setup.** `PunchGroup20::encode_die` writes the control-checked group records of #2961 with `ID_PUNCH,c_die` on each work. `PunchGroup20::encode` (PAIR20) keeps its bytes and its review text. The die review text tells the operator to confirm `c_die` on each work, to keep each pass inside its own opening, to check that no cutting move crosses the plate between the openings, and to support each slug.
- The example `examples/agie/die-pair.camscript` uses the current post name. The decision file is `docs/decisions/2977-wire-die-pair.md`. The user guide section "Group two die openings in one plate" has the control readings.

## Value sources

No setup value is new. Each value comes from a control-checked setup:

- The group records, the work order `CUT1`, `CUT2` and the SBR layout: PAIR20 (#2961).
- The die side `c_die` and the 20 mm rule for a die: DIE20 (#2957).
- The one CCB030 quality object: #2984.
- The 1 mm separation, steel 0001, Berco Cut 0.25 and the 20 mm offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm: the existing QN2 table (#2954).
- The plate, the two rims and the threading holes X-35.5 Y0 and X24.5 Y0: the example of this PR.

## Readings

The ported DUODI20 job was imported on the emulated Classic Cut 2S control (a throwaway clone of the practice image; the base image SHA-256 did not change). No physical cut was made.

- The two ISO files and the SBL arrived on the control byte for byte.
- After import: `CUT1` and `CUT2` show `CCB030[0]`. The formal check gave one error for each work: `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- Each work: quality CCB030 (Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0, Te 1.5, both options off), side **Matrijs**, separation 1.0, closed contour. Start holes X-35.500 Y0.000 and X24.500 Y0.000.
- TECCUT on `CUT1`: header `Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.30 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5`, row 0199, technology `estbca25nnn060b030020`. `CUT2` got the same T100. Offsets on each work: 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm. Both works then show `CCB030[4]`.
- The formal check of the piece: `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. The warnings are the same as for PAIR20: `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` on each work and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren`.
- GRAFICHECK (J00): ten cut blocks in this order: the main pass of `CUT1`, the main pass of `CUT2`, the separation of `CUT1`, the separation of `CUT2` (Y0 to Y1, 1.000 mm), the three trims of `CUT1`, the three trims of `CUT2`. The machine moves between the works only in transit blocks with the head up. All cutting points stay in their own opening: `CUT1` X-42.366 to X-17.634, `CUT2` X17.634 to X42.366. No cutting point is in the plate between the openings (X-17.5 to X17.5).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `agie_die_group_setup`: `die_group_files_match_the_control_checked_die_pair` (golden `DUODI20.SBL` and `DUODI20.SBR`), `each_opening_has_its_own_geometry_die_side_quality_and_hole`, `the_die_group_differs_from_the_punch_group_only_in_the_side`, `a_single_die_keeps_its_zero_step_setup` (DIE20), `a_die_group_refuses_other_heights_counts_and_repeated_stems`.
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::die_group_tests`: `a_die_pair_writes_an_iso_a_die_work_and_a_hole_for_each_opening`, `a_single_die_through_the_group_export_keeps_its_bytes`, `the_same_opening_twice_or_a_hole_in_the_other_opening_writes_nothing`, `the_band_between_openings_includes_the_lead_rough_corner_and_wire`, `a_die_group_refuses_another_height_or_no_separation`.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` `die::die_group`: `two_complete_rims_on_one_plate_post_the_control_checked_die_pair` (CLI output equals the goldens, with the ISO goldens `DUODI201.ISO` and `DUODI202.ISO`), `a_missing_shared_or_unsafe_die_work_writes_nothing` (same opening twice, one operation on a two-opening plate, hole in the other opening, a punch and a die, an extra model, slug not captured).
- The goldens that main already has (CCSEP20, DIE20 and the inspection goldens) do not change. Other goldens are listed in "Goldens moved". Existing tests pass unchanged.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head `1e12c77a4`: 1193 steps, 1 failed. The failed step is the known red `rotary_verify` `a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius` (#3774). This PR does not touch that code. The pinning tests above pass. The branch merges cleanly with the current `origin/main` (`git merge-tree`).

Strict clippy (`-D warnings`, all targets) on `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean. No heavy lane: this is not a `P1` PR.

## Not exercised

- No physical cut. The control check was offline.
- A die group with more than two openings (#2980), a mixed punch and die group, and a die group with CCB035 are refused. The control did not check them.
- The release of each slug on a real machine. The operator must support each slug, as the review text says.

Changelog: The native wire EDM post groups two through-openings of one retained 20 mm die plate in one job.

## UI screenshots

This PR contains the two open-cutoff controls of #2972 on the Wire Contour Passes tab. One pair of images covers all five PRs of the stack. The reviewer rendered the images with the crate's egui_kittest harness.

Before (main):

![Before: Wire Contour Passes tab on main](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr-2972/wire-open-cutoff-before.png?raw=true)

After (with the two cutoff controls):

![After: Wire Contour Passes tab with the two cutoff controls](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr-2972/wire-open-cutoff-after.png?raw=true)

## Goldens moved

The golden files below are additions relative to main. This PR changes no golden file that main already has. The goldens CCSEP20 and DIE20 of main do not change.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/CIRCLE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of a placed circle DXF job. Added by #2978 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/DUODI201.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of die opening 1 of the die pair. Added by #2981 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/DUODI202.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of die opening 2 of the die pair. Added by #2981 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/FINE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of the FINE20 job with quality CCB035. Added by #2979 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/FINE20.SBL` (A): pins the SBL of the FINE20 job with quality CCB035. Added by #2979 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/FINE20.SBR` (A): pins the SBR of the FINE20 job with quality CCB035. Added by #2979 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/RACE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of a placed racetrack DXF job. Added by #2978 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/DUODI20.SBL` (A): pins the SBL of a die pair on one retained plate. Added by #2981 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/DUODI20.SBR` (A): pins the SBR of a die pair on one retained plate. Added by #2981 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/LOWER20.SBL` (A): pins the open-cutoff (zero-step, one cut) setup SBL. Added by #2972 of the stack.

title: feat(wire): request the Ra 0.35 work quality for one 20 mm punch
body:
Stacked on #2978. Review the [quality changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/124be7caf9a9b37f79f34bf30394a7db6e765f89...17cb6f617460627b543f160f0e06821a752bac27).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR is ported onto the zero-step setup of #2984. The job names the requested work quality. It arms no technology. The operator assigns TECCUT on the control after the review, as for every other job.

- The new Wire Contour condition `AGIE_BERCO_RA035` requests quality `CCB035`: Ra 0.35, Te 1.50 and Tkm 1.00 µm, with the speed option set and the other two options disabled: `JE_CreateQuality(je_piece,"CCB035","0.35,1.50,1.00,T,F,F",je_q1)`. With the speed option, the control preselects the Ra 0.35 technology `estbca25nsn060b035020` (TECCUT header `TYPE:VS`). The job still arms no technology. The condition `AGIE_QN2` requests `CCB030`, as before.
- `camcraft_post::agie_setup::Quality` (`Ccb030`, `Ccb035`) is on the private `Piece`. The piece creates one quality object with that name. `PunchSetup20::encode_quality` is the only way to request `CCB035`. `encode`, `encode_die`, `PunchGroup20` and `CutoffSetup20` keep `CCB030`.
- `CCB035_OFFSETS_UM` has one row: 20 mm, five passes, 234, 189, 154, 139 and 129 µm (main cut and four trims). `Quality::offsets_um` returns all passes, and `Quality::rough_um` gives the main cut. The contour checks (clearance, miter and entry) use the main-cut offset of the selected quality: 234 µm for `CCB035`. The 0.4 mm stock margin does not change (0.234 + 0.125 rounds up to 0.4). `CCB030` keeps its 4-pass table and its bytes.
- The operator review of `CCB035` names the technology `estbca25nsn060b035020`, the header `TYPE:VS`, 5 passes and the five offsets. It tells the operator to stop if one of them is different. The user guide says the same. It names the technology, not a TECCUT number: the first TECCUT column is a match distance, not a row id.
- `camcraft_post::agie::export_punch_with_review` takes the quality. With `Ccb030` it is `export_with_review`.
- The app refuses `AGIE_BERCO_RA035` for a punch group and for a DXF circle or racetrack. The post refuses other stock thicknesses, a die opening and an open cutoff. No directory is written.
- The old script writer (`jescript.rs`) is gone on the frame. The old `AgieQuality` type is replaced by `Quality`.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2966-agie-fine-quality.md`. User guide: "Request Ra 0.35 µm for one 20 mm punch".

## Value sources

- Ra 0.35, Te 1.50 and Tkm 1.00: the Fine+ values of the MIT Agie Processor quality presets, as in the original PR.
- The speed flag and the offsets 234, 189, 154, 139 and 129 µm at 20 mm: the control measurement of 25 Nov (`Camcraft-notes/agie-imports-20261125/FINE20-0289/summary.txt`) and the control check of this head (below). The user decided the change.
- The quality name `CCB035` follows `CCB030` (#2984: a generic name can bind other resident data).

## Readings on the emulated Classic Cut 2S: the speed flag (folder 25 Nov)

Job `FINE20` from `examples/agie/fine-punch.camscript` on this head. These are the golden files. The SBL is byte-identical to the probe SBL of the 25 Nov measurement. Evidence: the maintainer's notes folder `agie-imports-20261125/FINE20-new/` (screenshots, J00, summary). Throwaway clone of `practice-color-ready`; the base image SHA-256 did not change.

- The ISO and the SBL arrived on the control byte for byte.
- After import: `CUT1 - CCB035[0]`. FORMALCHECK gave one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- Work Details: quality `CCB035`, Ra 0.35 µm, Tkm 1.0 µm, Te 1.5 µm, "Snelheid" (speed) on, "Hoge kwaliteit" off.
- TECCUT header: `M:x123 Mat:Fe Maf:BC TYPE:VS Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.35 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5`. The control preselected technology `estbca25nsn060b035020` (type S, 5 passes; shown with Dis 0199).
- After Assign, with no manual row choice: `CCB035[5]`, T100 on each pass, offsets 234 (main), 189, 154, 139 and 129 µm.
- FORMALCHECK: `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. With warnings on: `Uitgekozen opties : 131584` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.
- GRAFICHECK (J00, 9602 bytes): 5 passes in the main loop and 5 in the 1.000 mm separation. The face offsets are X ±20.234, ±20.189, ±20.154, ±20.139 and ±20.129, equal to the table. The J00 is byte-identical to the J00 of the 25 Nov probe.

## Earlier readings without the speed flag (2026-11-24, superseded)

Job `FINE20` from `examples/agie/fine-punch.camscript`. These are the golden files.

- The ISO and the SBL arrived on the control byte for byte.
- After import: `CUT1 - CCB035[0]`. FORMALCHECK gave one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- Work Details: quality `CCB035`, Ra 0.35 µm, Tkm 1.0 µm, Te 1.5 µm. The two visible options were off.
- TECCUT header: `M:x123 Mat:Fe Maf:BC TYPE:V Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.35 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5`.
- The control preselected row 0204: 4 passes, technology `estbca25nnn060b030020`. This is the Ra 0.30 technology that `CCB030` also preselects. The table also has row 0289, `estbca25nsn060b035020`: type S, 5 passes, Ra 0.35. The control did not preselect it. It was not assigned, and its offsets are not measured.
- After the assignment of row 0204: `CCB035[4]`, T100 on each pass, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.
- FORMALCHECK: `geen fouten`. With warnings on: `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.
- GRAFICHECK: the trace is the same as the trace of the 15 mm `CCB030` punch, except Z. The separation is 1.000 mm.

Result of that run: without the speed flag, the control preselected the Ra 0.30 technology. The speed flag above corrects this. No physical cut was made, so the surface Ra is not measured.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::quality_tests`:
  - `ccb035_changes_only_the_quality_line_of_a_20_mm_punch`
  - `ccb030_through_the_quality_export_keeps_every_byte`
  - `ccb035_refuses_other_heights_sides_and_separations_without_files`
  - `the_setup_encoder_holds_ccb035_to_20_mm`
- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::quality_tests::ccb035_has_five_measured_passes_and_keeps_the_0_4_mm_margin` (new: the 5-entry table, the main-cut offset and the 0.4 mm margin).
- `camcraft-app` test `agie_native`, module `quality` (moved from the binary `agie_quality`):
  - `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality` (save, load, FINE20 golden)
  - `ra035_refuses_unmeasured_heights_without_a_directory` (15, 40 and 80 mm)
  - `ra035_refuses_a_group_an_arc_punch_a_die_and_a_cutoff` (each example posts with `AGIE_QN2`, and is refused with `AGIE_BERCO_RA035`)
- The goldens that main already has (CCSEP20, DIE20 and the inspection goldens) do not change. Other goldens are listed in "Goldens moved". Existing tests pass unchanged.

## Gate (head `688f776e0`)

The head merges `origin/main` at `aedd9750c` (through the #2978 head), which has the fix of #3774.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: batch fallback (geometry is in the stack diff). 1201 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (42.1 min). `agie_native` (28 tests), `agie_safe_setup`, `script_agie_native`, `example_catalog*` and the `post`, `app` and `ui` lib tests passed.

title: feat(wire): post a selected DXF circle or racetrack punch with native arcs
body:
Stacked on #2974. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/04cec49fe...issue/2022-agie-placed-dxf).

Process change: yes

This PR now uses the #2984 zero-step setup writer and the #3180 selected-chain wire path. The port merged `04cec49fe` (#2974) into the branch. The branch merges cleanly with `main` (`git merge-tree`, no conflicts).

## What changed

A Wire Contour punch can use one selected closed DXF chain that is a circle or a racetrack. A racetrack has two straight lines that are tangent to two semicircles of the same radius. The native wire EDM post writes the nominal arcs as `G03` blocks with incremental `I`/`J` centres.

- `camcraft_geometry::wire_round_profile`: `RoundProfile::from_chain` reads the selected chain and proves the tangent joins, the radius and the joint gap. `preview()` gives a polygon that encloses each true arc with at most 0.000025 mm of radial excess.
- `operation/wire_sketch.rs`: `nominal_ring` gives the preview polygon to the generator and to the wire laws for a punch. A straight chain and a die keep the old behaviour. A die with arcs is still refused.
- `operation/agie_profile.rs`: the existing checks moved into `checked()`, with the same messages and order. `agie_sketch_job` adds the DXF punch. It checks the rest of the drawing against the native envelope (arc extrema plus 0.4 mm, and the full threading hole).
- `posting_agie.rs`: one selected DXF chain goes to `agie::export_round_with_review`. Other jobs use the group path as before.
- `post/src/agie/round_profile.rs`: native ISO blocks, the arc envelope bound and the refusals. The SBL and SBR come from `PunchSetup20::encode`.
- The examples select the closed chain through `list_features` and `set_operation_geometry`. They use the post name `Native wire EDM job files`.

Dropped from the old branch: the whole-drawing source (`SrcRef::Entity`) and its stamp, which #3180 replaces. Also dropped: the prism mesh, the `round_profile` field on `AgieJob` and the `jescript.rs` writer. The decision file has the reasons.

## Scope

In scope, as the control data of this PR supports:

- One racetrack punch with straight sides parallel to X or Y, and a perpendicular entry on a straight side.
- One circle punch from R6 to R15 with a horizontal or vertical radial entry.
- A 20 mm plate, a single work, and coordinates exactly on the five-decimal grid.

Out of scope, and refused visibly:

- A die opening with arcs (needs `c_die` and a control run).
- Other plate heights.
- A group with an arc work (`PunchGroup20` reads modeled punches only).
- Oblique racetracks and oblique holes (need a rounding proof and a control run).

## Setup field sources

No setup field is new. The SBL is `PunchSetup20::encode`, the control-checked `CCSEP20` punch of #2984. A test compares each SBL with `CCSEP20.SBL`: only the stem and the `stp1` position change. The stock (80 × 60 × 20 mm), the holes and the geometry come from the examples of this PR.

## Readings

Emulated Agie Classic Cut 2S, clone of `practice-color.qcow2` (SHA-256 `b827a383…` unchanged; clone deleted). Four jobs from head `124be7caf`: `RACE20`, `CIRCLE20` (R10, hole X−17 Y0), `NORTH15` (R15, hole X0 Y22) and `EAST6` (R6, hole X13 Y0). For each job:

- The tree shows `CCB030[0]` after import. FORMALCHECK gives one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- The quality is CCB030 with Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0 and Te 1.5. The TECCUT header is Dia 0.25, H20, Ra 0.30 (row 0199, `estbca25nnn060b030020`).
- After TECCUT: `CCB030[4]`, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm, and `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. The warnings are `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.

GRAFICHECK (J00):

- `RACE20`: all passes keep the arc centres (10, 1) and (−6, 1). The pass radii are 10.245, 10.155, 10.140 and 10.134 mm. The trims run in the opposite direction (`G02`). The separation on the straight is 1.000 mm (X2 to X1).
- Circles: all passes are concentric on (0, 0). The separation arc ends 1/R radians from the seam (0.100, 0.0667 and 0.1667 rad), a nominal arc of 1.000 mm.

These readings agree with the earlier control readings of this PR. No physical cut was made.

title: feat(wire): group independently captured punches in one native job
body:
Stacked on #2972. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/f99a9d736...issue/2961-agie-multiple-works).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR posts two independently captured punches on one 20 mm plate as one native wire EDM job. It is ported onto the zero-step setup writer of #2984 and onto the #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969 and #2972 ports. The old branch wrote its own SBL through `jescript.rs`. That writer is deleted on main, and this port does not use it.

- **Piece writer (post).** `agie_setup/piece.rs` now takes one `Piece` (stem, stock, height) and a list of `Work` (ISO stem, side, start point, exit point). It writes one quality `CCB030`, one group and the works `CUT1..n` in a loop. Each work refers to the same quality object (`ID_QUALITY,je_q1`) and has its own `ID_GEOMETRY`, `stp1` and `ASDELETE` call. The single-work SBL is byte-identical to before.
- **Group setup (post).** The new `agie_setup::PunchGroup20` takes the group stem, the stock, the 20 mm height and two `GroupPunch` entries (ISO stem and start hole). It refuses another number of works, a repeated or invalid ISO stem, a height other than 20 mm, stock outside the 350 × 250 mm span and a hole that is not completely inside the stock. The SBR has one resource line for each ISO.
- **Group export (post).** `agie::export_group_with_review` sends one job to `export_with_review` unchanged. Two jobs must be closed punches on the same 20 mm stock with a separation of 1.0 mm, and the job name has at most seven characters. Each work passes the full single-punch checks. The two cutting areas must have a clear band along X or Y. Each area includes the solid, the hole, the 3 mm lead, the longest rough miter (at least the rough offset of the thickness) and the 0.125 mm wire radius. The job has `<name>1.ISO`, `<name>2.ISO`, one SBR and one SBL, published in one directory rename.
- **App.** The post takes one or two active Wire Contour operations. Two operations must use the same setup and wire tool. Each must select a different complete modeled punch, and no other model can be present (`posting_agie_group.rs`). `agie_job` now receives its source model from the caller.
- **Docs and example.** New user-guide section "Group two captured punches", the example `examples/agie/punch-pair.camscript` (two models, `PAIR20`) and the decision file `docs/decisions/2961-agie-punch-group.md`.

## Setup fields and their sources

- All work fields are those of the control-checked zero-step punch of #2984 (golden `CCSEP20.SBL`). Only the work name, `ID_GEOMETRY` and the `stp1` position change for each work.
- The quality is created one time for the piece, as in #2984. The old branch created `QN2` and `QN3`, one name for each work. #2984 found that the control can bind different quality names to different resident data.
- One ISO for each work, the geometry, the stock (80 × 60 × 20 mm) and the holes (X-30 Y0 and X1 Y0) are those of this PR's original control-checked pair.

## Readings

- `PAIR20` from `camcraft-cli script examples/agie/punch-pair.camscript`: four files. The SBL is byte-identical to the new golden `PAIR20.SBL`.
- Emulated Agie Classic Cut 2S (offline clone of the practice control, deleted after the run):
  - The ISO and SBL bytes on the control disk match the export.
  - After import: `CUT1 CCB030[0] stp1 PAIR201.ISO` and `CUT2 CCB030[0] stp1 PAIR202.ISO`. FORMALCHECK gives one "Technologie : te definiëren" error for each work.
  - Each work shows CCB030 with Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0 and Te 1.5 and both options off. The CUT2 start point is X1.000 Y0.000, diameter 2.0.
  - TECCUT gives the row `0199` (Dia 0.25, H20, Ra 0.30) and the technology `estbca25nnn060b030020` on both works. The offsets are 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm on each work. The tree then shows `CCB030[4]` on each work.
  - FORMALCHECK after TECCUT: "Controleresultaat: geen fouten" for the piece and for each work. Warnings: "Uitgekozen opties : 131072" and "Referentiewaarden : te definiëren" on each work, and "Bewerkingen : te definiëren" on the piece. A single-work job of the same frame (`SOLO20`) gives the same piece warnings.
  - GRAFICHECK: 16 cut blocks. The control cuts the four profile passes of CUT1, then of CUT2, then the four separation passes of CUT1, then of CUT2. Each separation is 1.000 mm. The moves between the works are only transit blocks (`TRA`, G00 with the head up). The cutting envelopes are CUT1 X-30.000..-9.755 Y-8.245..8.245 and CUT2 X1.000..24.245 Y-7.245..9.245. They do not touch.
- No physical cut was made.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup` (module `group`): `group_files_match_the_zero_step_punch_pair` (golden `PAIR20.SBL` and `PAIR20.SBR`), `each_work_has_its_own_geometry_side_and_hole`, `each_work_of_a_group_has_the_records_of_a_single_punch`, `a_group_refuses_its_unqualified_inputs`.
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::group_tests`: `a_punch_pair_writes_an_iso_a_resource_line_a_work_and_a_hole_for_each_punch`, `a_single_work_through_the_group_export_keeps_its_bytes` (equal to `CCSEP20.SBL`), `a_group_rejects_an_unqualified_height_or_reserved_geometry_alias`, `a_group_refuses_a_die_three_works_another_stock_or_no_separation`, `the_band_between_punches_includes_the_rough_corner_lead_and_wire`.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native`: `group::the_two_model_owners_have_distinct_programs_holes_and_captures`, `group::a_shared_source_an_unowned_model_or_a_crossing_thread_path_writes_nothing`.
- The goldens that main already has (CCSEP20, DIE20 and the inspection goldens) do not change. Other goldens are listed in "Goldens moved". Existing tests pass unchanged.

## Gate (head `0f39ce973`)

The head merges `origin/main` at `aedd9750c`, which has the fix of #3774.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 526 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (56.0 min). All `agie*` suites, `example_catalog*` and the `post`, `app` and `ui` lib tests pass.

## Goldens moved

The golden files below are additions relative to main. This PR changes no golden file that main already has. The goldens CCSEP20 and DIE20 of main do not change.

title: feat(wire): post a straight open cutoff with separate air endpoints
body:
Stacked on #2969. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/d3443eddc...issue/2962-agie-straight-cutoff).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR adds one straight open cutoff to the native wire EDM job files post. It is ported onto the zero-step setup writer of #2984 and onto the #2955, #2964, #2968 and #2969 ports. The old branch wrote its own SBL through `jescript.rs`. That writer is deleted on main, and this port does not use it.

- **Selection (app).** A Wire Contour with `side: left` or `side: right` takes one selected straight wall edge of the full-height retained prism. The edge must cross between opposite stock faces. The whole model must be on the side away from the kerf, inside the stock. The operation must state `both_pieces_restrained` and `stock_centered_in_xy_travel`, have no `start`, and have a run-out `clearance` of 3.6 mm or less (`crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`). A closed cycle still needs `capture` and a start hole.
- **New operation fields.** `both_pieces_restrained` and `stock_centered_in_xy_travel` are on `WireContourOp`, the project file (default false, so old files load unchanged), the Passes page and the MCP field list. Every other constructor, including the sketch-chain die of main, states them as false.
- The goldens that main already has (CCSEP20, DIE20 and the inspection goldens) do not change. Other goldens are listed in "Goldens moved". Existing tests pass unchanged.
- **Routing and separation (post).** `export_with_review` sends a left or right job to `cutoff::prepare`, which returns the ISO line and the setup. The separation rule is: 0.0 for an open cut, 1.0 for a closed cycle. A closed cycle with 0.0 is still refused.
- **Geometry (post).** The ISO is the nominal line, extended 4 mm into air at each end. The entry and exit points are 3 mm to the waste side of the tail ends. The post checks the stock corners and the centered 350 × 250 mm travel with the 20 mm rough offset plus the wire radius.
- **Text.** The refusals, the CPS description, the user guide and the `camcraft-mcp` skill row name the open cutoff, beside the reentrant and die text. The guide uses the 20 mm offset row for a cutoff. No new user-facing text uses the vendor name as a feature or post name (#3537).
- **Examples.** `examples/agie/cutoff-lower.camscript` (`LOWER20`, left) and `examples/agie/cutoff-upper.camscript` (`UPPER20`, right) on original 80 × 60 × 20 mm stock.

## Readings

Offline control import on 2026-11-24 (throwaway clone of `practice-color-ready`; the base image SHA-256 did not change). Evidence (screenshots, J00 plots and the imported CamCraft files) is in the maintainer's notes folder `agie-imports-20261123/LOWER20/` and `UPPER20/`. The head of this PR posts the same bytes.

- Import: ISO and SBL bytes on the control match the CamCraft files. The new piece shows `CUT1 - CCB030[0], stp1+stp2`.

- FORMALCHECK after TECCUT: `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. With warnings: `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.
- GRAFICHECK (J00): four passes, each one crossing of the 88 mm line, in alternate directions. LOWER20 at Y −5.755, −5.845, −5.860 and −5.866. UPPER20 at Y 5.755, 5.845, 5.860 and 5.866. Each pass starts and ends at X±44 Y∓3 in air. These are the values of the earlier control run of this PR. The `PKT` marker 3 mm after the entry is the technology change point, as in the accepted DIE20 plot.

title: feat(wire): post a selected convex through die opening as native wire EDM job files
body:
Stacked on #2968. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1962fd5dc...issue/2957-agie-die-opening).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR adds a die opening to the native wire EDM job files post. It is ported onto the zero-step setup of #2984, the measured heights of #2964 and the reentrant checks of #2968. The old branch wrote its own SBL through `jescript.rs`. That writer is deleted on main, and this port does not use it.

- **Selection (app).** A Wire Contour with `side: die` takes the edge chains of the upper rim of one through-opening in one retained plate. CamCraft compares the picked rim with the full-height opening of the closed vertical prism. An outer rim, an incomplete rim and a blind floor are refused (`crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`).
- **Die setup (post).** `PunchSetup20::encode_die` writes the zero-step setup of `encode` with one changed field: `ID_PUNCH,c_die`. It refuses every thickness other than 20 mm (`SetupError::UnqualifiedDieHeight`). The controller review adds a check of the c_die side, the inward offsets and the slug support. The punch output does not change.
- **Mirrored geometry (post).** A die opening must be convex. The post reverses it to clockwise, so the retained plate is on the left and the waste on the right, as for a punch. The envelope check (renamed `check_cut_envelope`) then offsets toward the waste inside the opening. Its `cross < 0` test marks each opening corner as an inside corner of the plate. The reach check and `check_feature_spacing` use the rough offset of the selected thickness. The ISO object is reversed again after the seam, so the control reads a counter-clockwise opening that starts at the entry point.
- **Mirrored entry (post).** The entry code moves to `crates/post/src/agie/contour/entry.rs`. For a die, the complete 2 mm hole must lie inside each wall. The chosen wall needs 3 mm of lead and 3 mm of straight wall on each side of the foot. The foot must clear each other wall by the swept margin (0.4 mm at 20 mm). A punch keeps the supporting exterior face rule.
- **Text.** The refusals, the CPS description, the user guide and the `camcraft-mcp` skill row name the die opening. No new user-facing text uses the vendor name as a feature or post name (#3537).
- **Example.** `examples/agie/die-plate.camscript` posts the `DIE20` job from an original 60 × 60 × 20 mm plate with a 38-sided opening.

## Readings

- Earlier offline control run (comment of 2026-11-20, old writer): Agie Control plotted all 38 faces at the inward offsets 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. It cut the main profile and a 1.000 mm rough separation at X−12.255, then made three full trims. The threading point stayed at X−5.5 Y0. FORMALCHECK reported zero job errors. These offsets are the 20 mm row of `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`.
- This port (CLI, `die-plate.camscript`): 41 moves, no warning, 760.19 mm² of captured waste. `DIE20.ISO` starts at `G00 X-12.50000 Y0.00000`, then `G01 X-12.50000 Y-6.00000` (counter-clockwise). `DIE20.SBL` is byte-identical to the control-checked `CCSEP20.SBL`, except the stem, the stock (70 × 70 mm at X−35 Y−35), the start hole (X−5.5 Y0) and `ID_PUNCH,c_die`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup`: `die_setup_is_the_zero_step_punch_setup_with_the_die_side` (golden `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/DIE20.SBL`), `die_setup_is_refused_on_every_thickness_but_20_mm`.
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::die_tests`: `a_die_enters_the_nearest_wall_from_inside_and_keeps_counter_clockwise_iso`, `a_die_hole_too_close_to_one_wall_enters_the_opposite_wall`, `a_die_hole_must_lie_completely_inside_the_opening`, `the_same_ring_with_an_inside_hole_is_refused_as_a_punch`, `the_reach_check_flips_every_opening_corner_to_an_inside_corner`, `a_reentrant_die_opening_is_refused`, `a_die_needs_the_rough_pass_and_wire_margin_to_the_stock`, `a_die_requires_the_qualified_20_mm_plate`, `a_die_publishes_the_zero_step_setup_with_the_die_side`.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` (`die` module, the ported PR tests): `the_selected_die_rim_posts_nominal_walls_and_inward_compensation` (compares the CLI SBL with the `DIE20.SBL` golden), `an_outer_rim_an_external_pierce_or_an_incomplete_rim_cannot_publish_a_die`, `a_blind_floor_under_the_selected_upper_rim_cannot_publish_a_die`.
- All #2955, #2964 and #2968 tests stay green without changes to their assertions.

## Gate (head `d3443eddc`)

Head `d3443eddc` merges the #2968 head `6443d4f09` into `30e6c4c3f`. That head contains `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3219). No rebase and no force-push.

Conflicts and resolution:
- `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`: no conflict in this merge. The #2964 merge already resolved it: the `inspection` and `publish` modules of `main` come first, then `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`. `encode_die` and `ID_PUNCH,c_die` stay unchanged.
- `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, the Wire Contour row: the die text of this PR and the reentrant text of #2968 are both kept.
- `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`, steps 3 and 4 of the control check: step 3 uses the row of the selected stock thickness (from #2964) and says that a die plate uses the 20 mm row. Step 4 keeps the die text of this PR. Step 1 says that a die is 20 mm only. The die corner text names the 20 mm row for the 0.245 mm offset.

Results:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: batch plan, 1189 steps in 33.7 min, 1 failed, 0 stalled.
  - The red step is `app suites: rotary_verify`, `a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius` (2110 against 2064). This is the known red of `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3774, follow-up #3794). This PR does not change rotary code.
  - Green: `clippy -D warnings`, `post suites: agie_inspection` (2), `agie_safe_setup` (8), `script_agie_native` (11), `app suites: agie_native` (16), `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Posted bytes: no file under `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/` (`CCSEP20.SBL`, `DIE20.SBL`) changed against `30e6c4c3f`. `agie_safe_setup` and `agie_native` pass.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree d3443eddc origin/main` (`940cc5d0e`): clean.

## Not exercised

- The offline control import of the zero-step `DIE20` job ran on 2026-11-23 from head `30e6c4c3f`: see [the DIE20 control result](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2969#issuecomment-7115465528). It reported zero steps at import, the c_die side, inward offsets, the 1 mm separation, three trims and no FORMALCHECK error after TECCUT. The merge of `d3443eddc` does not change a posted byte. The control is an emulation, not the installed machine.
- No physical cut was made.
- Die thicknesses other than 20 mm and non-convex openings are refused. They have no control data.
- Heavy lanes were not run (P6).

Effort: high
Changelog: The native wire EDM job files post accepts a selected convex through-opening in a 20 mm plate. It writes the zero-step setup with the die side and checks the retained plate, the inward lead and the rough offset before it writes the job.

Fixes #2957

title: feat(post): add Hurco WinMax (NC) ISNC post and Hurco VM10i machine
body:
Replaces #2640 with the same Hurco commit (`4cd8bdae2`, cherry-picked unchanged) on a branch straight off `main`. #2640 was stacked on the Grbl post draft #2506, so it could not merge before #2506; this one does not need it.

## Latest review fixes

Head: `ed04216dc468f9880dea0651c813b5762c401488`.

- Finding 1: Cancel active cycles before travel. Seat each hole at the section hop before descent to R. Refuse missing hops.
- The `cycle_hop` suite includes Hurco. It checks back-to-back cycles and cycles after probing, feeds, and arcs.
- Finding 3: Set the vendor to `Camcraft`. `hurco_post_vendor_is_camcraft` pins the value.
- All 30 focused tests passed. Cycle seating, feed tracking, arc tracking, and vendor mutations failed their pins. Restored fixes passed.
- Update the synthesized Hurco golden for safe hops. Conformance passed all 7 tests.
- Clippy for `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app`, all targets with warnings denied: passed.
- Quick gate ran 648 steps. After the golden update, only `continuous_4axis_part` remains red: `/version: 71 != 70`.
- Finding 2 remains open. No simulator access, load results, or path comparisons are available. Issue #2573 remains incomplete.

Re-checked on this branch: `camcraft-post --test script_hurco_winmax` 11 passed; `camcraft-app --test hurco_winmax_post` 7, `post_spindle_rule_all` 2, `conformance` 5 passed.

---

## What changed

- Add clean-room built-in post `Hurco WinMax (NC)` in `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps`.
- Add clean-room 3-axis VMC definition `Hurco VM10i` in `assets/machines/hurco-vm10i.mch`.
- Register both entries in `BUILTINS`, `MACHINES`, and `embedded()` inside `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`.
- Emit Hurco WinMax ISNC blocks (`G20`/`G21` unit block, `O0001`..`O9999`, `G90 G17 G94 G54..G59 G40 G49 G80`, `G54.1 P1`..`P93`, decimal-second `P` dwell on `G04`/`G82`/`G89`, `G84.2`/`G84.3` rigid tapping and `G84` floating tapping, `G68`/`G69` rotation, `G31` probing with `G10 L2`, no `G91.1`).
- Record design decisions in `docs/decisions/2573-hurco-winmax-post.md`.

## Cause

No built-in post processor or machine definition existed for Hurco WinMax 3-axis NC/ISO (ISNC) mills.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `crates/post/tests/hurco_winmax_post.rs` (8/8 pass; red before fix `0/7`: `hurco-winmax.cps` missing): multi-op contour/arc/drill/peck/tap across two tools and two offsets, `G20`/`G21` and `EndUnits`, decimal-second `P` dwell, `G84.2`/`G84.3`/`G84`, `G54`..`G59` and `G54.1 P1`..`P93`, `G28`/`G53` safe retract, `O0001`..`O9999` bounds, `G41`/`G42` compensation, `G68`/`G69` rotation, `G31` probing, smoothing note, named refusals, and a strict documented WinMax ISNC word-set allowlist check over posted programs and all 21 `.nc` goldens.
  - `crates/app/tests/hurco_winmax_post.rs` (2/2 pass; red before fix `0/2`: missing registry entries): checks `BUILTINS`/`MACHINES` registration, `post_serves`, VM10i parse, full ECS contour/pocket/drill/peck/rigid-tap workflow across two tools and `G54`/`G55`, plus `G54.1 P1`.
  - Cross-post suites updated and green: `conformance` (7/7), `machine` (33/33), `machine_library` (11/11), `post_spindle_rule_all` (5/5), `bore_cycle` (9/9), `comp_plane` (3/3), `decimal_point_fanuc_family` (3/3), `declared_options` (3/3), `end_units` (3/3), `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` (9/9), `radius_arcs` (7/7), `script_hurco_winmax` (11/11).
- Mutations (each verified RED when reverted/weakened, GREEN when restored):
  - `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` reverted to `HEAD`: `0/1` (`hurco_winmax_post_and_vm10i_are_registered_and_serve_mill` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `oWord()` `1..=9999` check removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `workOffsetMax` raised and `> 99` guard removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `G53` missing `safeRetractZ` check removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `rigidTapping === false` check removed: `0/1` (`tapping_modes_and_rigid_tapping_guard` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - Cycle illegal dwell `rawDwell > 0` check removed: `0/1` (`cycles_refuse_illegal_dwell_and_tilt_and_zero_spindle` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `tiltOk()` 3-axis guard bypassed: `0/1` (`cycles_refuse_illegal_dwell_and_tilt_and_zero_spindle` fails), restored `1/1`.
- Gate & lint:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 643 step(s), 0 failed (57.0 min).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: 0 warnings, exit 0.

## Goldens moved

- Added 14 new `conformance` goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/hurco-winmax/*.nc` (13 ops) and `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_hurco-winmax.nc`.
- Added 11 new `script_hurco_winmax` recorded goldens under `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/hurco-winmax/` (7 `.nc`, 4 `.refusal`).
- No existing `.nc` or `.cl` goldens changed.

## Not exercised

Latest review finding 2 remains open. The required simulator load results and path comparisons are not available. Issue #2573 remains incomplete.

Programs were not verified on the community owner's WinMax `09.01.393.30` simulator or on a physical Hurco control. Behaviour follows published Hurco WinMax Mill NC documentation (`704-0116-101`, `support.hurco.com`) and public Hurco VM10i specifications.

## Overlaps

This PR branches from `main`. It touches these functions and tables:
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (`BUILTINS`, `MACHINES`, `embedded`)
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` (`POSTS`, `EXTENSIONS`)
- `crates/app/tests/machine.rs` (`every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration`)
- `crates/app/tests/post_spindle_rule_all.rs` (`POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (`NO_DWELL`)
- `crates/post/tests/comp_plane.rs` (`POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/decimal_point_fanuc_family.rs` (`MILL_POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/declared_options.rs` (`shipped_milling_posts_declare_valid_option_schemas`)
- `crates/post/tests/end_units.rs` (`writing_mill_posts_emit_end_unit_word_before_program_end`)
- `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family.rs` (`POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/radius_arcs.rs` (`RADIUS_POSTS`)

Open PRs `#2515` and `#2310` also touch `posting_files.rs` / `conformance.rs` / `machine.rs` and were already conflicting with `main` at Step 2.

Changelog: Add built-in Hurco WinMax (NC) ISNC 3-axis mill post and Hurco VM10i machine.
Refs #2573
